Those who heard were moved with grief and said to one another, "The Tathāgata established the Dharma to guide and entice according to the capacity of the individual; we have clung to our ignorance and followed the gradual teachings. The Mahāyāna is the true principle; we should change our former attachments and strive to follow the holy will. This goose has handed down a warning and is truly a bright guide; we should commemorate its great virtue and transmit this record for all eternity." Thereupon, they built a stūpa to manifest its heroic legacy, burying the dead goose beneath it.

zh: 因陀羅勢羅窶訶山東北行百五六十里，至迦布德迦（唐言鴿）伽藍，僧徒二百餘人，學說一切有部。伽藍東有窣堵波，無憂王之所建也。昔佛於此為諸大眾一宿說法。時有羅者於此林中網捕羽族，一日不獲，遂作是言：「我惟薄福，恒為弊事。」來至佛所，揚言唱曰：「今日如來於此說法，令我網捕都無所得，妻孥飢餓，其計安出？」如來告曰：「汝應蘊火，當與汝食。」如來是時化作大鴿，投火而死，羅者持歸，妻孥共食。其後重往佛所，如來方便攝化，羅者聞法，悔過自新，捨家修學，便證聖果。因名所建為鴿伽藍。
en_current: Traveling northeast from the Indraśailaguhā (因陀羅勢羅窶訶) Mountain for one hundred and fifty or sixty li, one reaches the Kapotaka (迦布德迦; in Chinese, "pigeon") Monastery, where there are over two hundred monks who study the teachings of the Sarvāstivāda school. To the east of the monastery is a stūpa built by King Aśoka. In the past, the Buddha stayed here for one night to preach the Dharma to the great assembly. At that time, a fowler was netting birds in this forest; having caught nothing all day, he said, "I have but little merit and am always met with misfortune." He came to where the Buddha was and cried out, "Today the Tathāgata is preaching the Dharma here, causing me to catch nothing in my nets; my wife and children are starving, so what plan can I devise?" The Tathāgata replied, "You should kindle a fire, and I will provide you with food." The Tathāgata then transformed himself into a large pigeon and threw himself into the fire to die; the fowler took it home, and he and his wife and children ate it together. Afterward, he returned to the Buddha, who guided and transformed him through skillful means. The fowler heard the Dharma, repented of his faults, renewed himself, left home to study, and subsequently attained the holy fruit. For this reason, the monastery that was built there was named the Pigeon Monastery.

zh: 迦布德迦伽藍南二三里，至孤山。其山崇峻，樹林欝茂，名花清流，被崖緣壑。上多精舍靈廟，頗極剞劂之工。正中精舍有觀自在菩薩像，軀量雖小，威神感肅，手執蓮花，頂戴佛像。常有數人，斷食要心，求見菩薩，七日、二七日、乃至一月，其有感者，見觀自在菩薩，妙相莊嚴，威光赫奕，從像中出，慰喻其人。昔南海僧伽羅國王清旦以鏡照面，不見其身，乃覩贍部洲摩揭陀國多羅林中小山上有此菩薩像，王深感慶，圖以營求。既至此山，寔唯肖似，因建精舍，興諸供養。自後諸王尚想遺風，遂於其側建立精舍靈廟，香花伎樂供養不絕。
en_current: Two or three li south of the Kapotaka monastery (迦布德迦伽藍), one arrives at an isolated hill (孤山). The mountain is lofty and steep, with lush forests, famous flowers, and clear streams covering the cliffs and lining the ravines. Above, there are many vihāras (精舍) and sacred temples, which are extremely refined in their craftsmanship. In the central vihāra is a statue of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara (觀自在菩薩); although small in size, its spiritual majesty inspires awe, as it holds a lotus in its hand and bears a Buddha figure upon its crown. There are often people who fast and focus their minds, seeking a vision of the Bodhisattva for seven days, fourteen days, or even a full month; those who receive a response see the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, in all his solemn and wondrous beauty and brilliant radiance, emerge from the statue to comfort and exhort them. Long ago, the king of Siṃhala (僧伽羅國) in the South Sea looked into a mirror at dawn and saw not his own reflection, but rather this Bodhisattva statue atop a small hill in the Tāla forest of Magadha (摩揭陀國) in Jambudvīpa (贍部洲); the king, deeply moved and joyful, sought to find it. When he arrived at this hill, he found the statue to be exactly as he had seen, so he built a vihāra and established various offerings. Since then, subsequent kings, admiring this legacy, have built vihāras and sacred temples alongside it, and offerings of incense, flowers, and music have never ceased.

name_zh: 一伽藍 (孤山東南四十餘里)
zh: 孤山觀自在菩薩像東南行四十餘里，至一伽藍，僧徒五十餘人，並學小乘法教。伽藍前有大窣堵波，多有靈異，佛昔於此為梵天王等七日說法。其側則有過去三佛坐及經行遺迹之所。
en_current: Traveling southeast for more than forty li from the statue of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara (觀自在菩薩) on the isolated hill (孤山), one reaches a monastery where there are more than fifty monks, all of whom study the teachings of the Hīnayāna. In front of the monastery is a great stūpa, which possesses many miraculous qualities; it is the place where the Buddha formerly preached the Dharma for seven days to the Brahmadeva-rāja and others. Beside it are the sites of the traces of the sitting and walking meditation of the three past Buddhas.

zh: 伽藍東北行七十餘里，殑伽河南，至大聚落，人民殷盛，有數天祠，並窮彫飾。東南不遠有大窣堵波，佛昔於此一宿說法。
en_current: Traveling northeast from the monastery for more than seventy li, to the south of the Ganges (Gaṅgā) River, one arrives at a large settlement where the population is dense and prosperous. There are several deva temples, all of which are exquisitely carved and adorned. Not far to the southeast is a great stupa (stūpa), where the Buddha once stayed for one night and preached the Dharma.

zh: 從此東入山林中，行百餘里，至落般膩羅聚落。伽藍前有大窣堵波，無憂王之所建，佛昔於此三月說法。此北二三里有大池，周三十餘里，四色蓮花四時開發。從此東入大山林中，行二百餘里，至伊爛拏鉢伐多國（中印度境）。
en_current: From here, traveling east into the mountains and forests for more than one hundred li, one reaches the village of Luobanniluo (Röhinila). In front of the monastery is a great stupa built by King Ashoka (Aśoka), where the Buddha once stayed for three months to preach the Dharma. Two or three li to the north of this place is a large pond, more than thirty li in circumference, where four-colored lotus flowers bloom in all four seasons. From here, traveling east into the great mountains and forests for more than two hundred li, one reaches the country of Yilannabafaduo (Hiraṇyaparvata) (within the borders of Central India).

zh: 此伽藍南菴沒羅林中有池，其龍名那爛陀，傍建伽藍，因取為稱。
en_current: To the south of this monastery (saṃghārāma), in a mango grove (āmra-vana), there is a pond; its dragon (nāga) is named Nālandā, and because the monastery was built beside it, it took its name from this.

zh: 其南則有觀自在菩薩立像。或見執香爐往佛精舍，周旋右繞。
en_current: To the south of it there is a standing statue of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara (觀自在菩薩). Sometimes he is seen holding an incense burner, proceeding to the Buddha *vihāra* (佛精舍), and circumambulating it to the right.

zh: 觀自在菩薩像南窣堵波中，有如來三月之間剃剪髮、爪。有嬰疾病，旋繞多愈。
en_current: To the south of the statue of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara (觀自在菩薩) is a stūpa containing the hair and fingernails of the Tathāgata, shorn and clipped over a period of three months. Those afflicted with illness who circumambulate it are mostly healed.

zh: 觀自在菩薩精舍北有大精舍，高三百餘尺，婆羅阿迭多王之所建也，莊嚴度量及中佛像，同菩提樹下大精舍。
en_current: To the north of the Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva Vihāra (觀自在菩薩精舍) is a great vihāra, over three hundred feet high, which was built by King Bālāditya (婆羅阿迭多王); its ornamentation, dimensions, and the Buddha image within are identical to those of the great vihāra under the Mahā-bodhi (菩提樹).

zh: 次東二百餘步垣外，有銅立佛像，高八十餘尺，重閣六層，乃得彌覆，昔滿胄王之所作也。
en_current: Further east, more than two hundred paces outside the wall, there is a standing copper image of the Buddha, over eighty feet high; it is sheltered by a six-story pavilion, and was made by King Pūrṇavarman (滿胄王) in the past.

name_zh: 帝釋窟東峯伽藍・亘娑窣堵波
zh: 東峯上有伽藍，聞諸土俗曰：其中僧眾，或於夜分，望見西峯石室佛像前每有燈炬，常為照燭。因陀羅勢羅窶訶山東峯伽藍前有窣堵波，謂亘（許贈反）娑（唐言雁）。昔此伽藍習翫小乘，小乘漸教也，故開三淨之食，而此伽藍遵而不墜。其後三淨求不時獲。有比丘經行，忽見群雁飛翔，戲言曰：「今日眾僧中食不充，摩訶薩埵宜知是時。」言聲未絕，一雁退飛，當其僧前，投身自殞。比丘見已，具白眾僧，聞者悲感，咸相謂曰：「如來設法，導誘隨機；我等守愚，遵行漸教。大乘者，正理也，宜改先執，務從聖旨。此雁垂誡，誠為明導，宜旌厚德，傳記終古。」於是建窣堵波，式昭遺烈，以彼死雁瘞其下焉。
en_current: On the eastern peak there is a monastery. I heard from the local people that the monks there sometimes see, during the night, lamps and torches constantly shining as illumination before the Buddha image in the stone chamber on the western peak. In front of the monastery on the eastern peak of the mountain of Indraśailaguhā (因陀羅勢羅窶訶山), there is a stūpa called Haṃsa (亘娑; 亘 read 許贈反; in Chinese, "wild goose"). Formerly, this monastery studied and practiced the Lesser Vehicle (Hīnayāna), which is the gradual teaching; therefore, it permitted the consumption of the three pure meats, and this monastery followed this practice without fail. Later, the three pure meats were not always obtainable. A bhikṣu was walking in meditation when he suddenly saw a flock of geese flying by and said in jest, "Today the monks do not have enough for their midday meal; the Mahāsattva should know that now is the time." Before his voice had ceased, one goose flew back, landed in front of the monk, and cast its body down, dying on the spot. When the bhikṣu saw this, he reported the details to the assembly of monks. Those who heard were moved to sorrow and all said to one another, "The Tathāgata established the Dharma to guide beings according to their capacities; we, clinging to our ignorance, have followed the gradual teaching. The Great Vehicle (Mahāyāna) is the correct principle; we should change our former attachments and strive to follow the holy intent. This goose has offered a warning and is truly a clear guide; we should honor its great virtue and record it for all time." Thereupon, they built a stūpa to manifest its legacy and buried the dead goose beneath it.

name_zh: 頻毘娑羅王迎見佛處窣堵波
zh: 沒特伽羅子故里東行三四里，有窣堵波，頻毘娑羅王迎見佛處。如來初證佛果，知摩揭陀國人心渴仰，受頻毘娑羅王請，於晨朝時，著衣持鉢，與千比丘左右圍繞，皆是耆舊螺髻梵志，慕法染衣，前後羽從，入王舍城。時帝釋天王變為摩那婆，首冠螺髻，左手執金瓶，右手持寶杖，足蹈空虛，離地四指，在大眾中前導佛路。時摩揭陀國頻毘娑羅王與其國內諸婆羅門、長者、居士，百千萬眾，前後導從，出王舍城奉迎聖眾。
en_current: Going E 3 or 4 li from the native village of Maudgalyāyana (沒特伽羅子), there is a stūpa, the place where King Bimbisāra (頻毘娑羅王) met the Buddha. When the Tathāgata had first attained Buddhahood, knowing that the people of Magadha (摩揭陀國) longed for him with thirsting hearts, he accepted King Bimbisāra's invitation; in the early morning he put on his robe and took his bowl and, surrounded on both sides by a thousand bhikṣus, all of them formerly aged brahmins with coiled hair who out of longing for the Dharma had put on the dyed robe, attending him in front and behind, he entered Rājagṛha (王舍城). At that time Śakra (帝釋), king of the gods, transformed himself into a māṇava (摩那婆), his head crowned with coiled hair, holding a golden flask in his left hand and a jewelled staff in his right; treading on empty air four fingers' breadth above the ground, he went in the midst of the great assembly, leading the way before the Buddha. At that time King Bimbisāra of Magadha, with the brahmins, elders and householders of his country, a multitude of hundreds of thousands of myriads leading and following him, went out of Rājagṛha to welcome the holy assembly.

name_zh: 舍利子門人入涅槃處窣堵波
zh: 迦羅臂挐迦邑東南四五里，有窣堵波，是尊者舍利子門人入涅槃處。或曰：迦葉波佛在世時，有三拘胝（拘胝者，唐言億）大阿羅漢同於此地無餘寂滅。
en_current: 4 or 5 li SE of the village of Kālapināka (迦羅臂挐迦邑) there is a stūpa, the place where the disciples of the venerable Śāriputra (舍利子) entered nirvāṇa. Some say that when Kāśyapa Buddha (迦葉波佛) was in the world, three koṭis (a koṭi is in Chinese 億) of great arhats entered final nirvāṇa without remainder together at this place.

zh: 伊爛拏鉢伐多國，周三千餘里。國大都城北臨殑伽河，周二十餘里。稼穡滋植，花菓具繁。氣序和暢，風俗淳質。伽藍十餘所，僧徒四千餘人，多學小乘正量部法。天祠二十餘所，異道雜居。近有隣王廢其國君，以大都城持施眾僧。於此城中建二伽藍，各減千僧，並學小乘教說一切有部。大城側，臨殑伽河，有伊爛拏山，含吐烟霞，蔽虧日月，古今仙聖繼踵棲神，今有天祠尚遵遺則。在昔如來亦嘗居此，為諸天、人廣說妙法。大城南有窣堵波，如來於此三月說法。其傍則有過去三佛坐及經行遺迹之所。三佛經行西不遠，有窣堵波，是室縷多頻設底拘胝（唐言聞二百億。舊譯曰億耳，謬也）苾芻生處。昔此城有長者，豪貴巨富，晚有繼嗣，時有報者，輒賜金錢二百億，因名其子聞二百億。洎乎成立，未曾履地，故其足跖毛長尺餘，光潤細軟，色若黃金。珍愛此兒，備諸玩好，自其居家以至雪山，亭傳連隅，僮僕交路，凡須妙藥，遞相告語，轉而以授，曾不踰時，其豪富如此。世尊知其善根將發，也命沒特伽羅子而往化焉。既至門下，莫由自通。長者家祠日天，每晨朝時東向以拜。是時尊者以神通力，從日輪中降立於前。長者子疑日天也，因施香飯而歸，其飯香氣遍王舍城。時頻毘娑羅王駭其異馥，命使歷問，乃竹林精舍沒特伽羅子自長者家持來，因知長者子有此奇異，乃使召焉。長者承命，思何安步？泛舟鼓棹，有風波之危；乘車馭象，懼蹶躓之患。於是自其居家，至王舍城，鑿渠通漕，流滿芥子，御舟安止，長縆以引。至王舍城，先禮世尊。世尊告曰：「頻毘娑羅王命使召汝，無過欲見足下毛耳。王欲觀者，宜結跏坐。伸脚向王，國法當死。」長者子受誨而往，引入廷謁。王欲視毛，乃跏趺坐，王善其有禮，特深珍愛。亦既得歸，還至佛所。如來是時說法誨喻，聞而感悟，遂即出家。於是精勤修習，思求果證，經行不捨，足遂流血。世尊告曰：「汝善男子，在家之時知鼓琴耶？」曰：「知。」「若然者，以此為喻。絃急則聲不合韻，絃緩則調不和雅，非急非緩，其聲乃和。夫修行者亦然。急則身疲心怠，緩則情舒志逸。」承佛指教，奉以周旋，如是不久，便獲果證。
en_current: The country of Īraṇaparvata (伊爛拏鉢伐多國) is over three thousand *li* in circuit. The capital city of the country borders the Gaṅgā River to the north and is over twenty *li* in circuit. The crops are lush and productive, and flowers and fruits are abundant. The climate is mild and pleasant, and the customs are honest and simple. There are more than ten monasteries with over four thousand monks, most of whom study the teachings of the Hīnayāna Saṃmitīya school. There are more than twenty deva temples where followers of various heterodox sects live together. Recently, a neighboring king deposed the ruler of this country and bestowed the capital city upon the community of monks. Within this city, two monasteries were built, each housing nearly one thousand monks, both of which study the Hīnayāna Sarvāstivāda school.  Beside the great city, overlooking the Gaṅgā River, is Mount Īraṇa, which exhales mists and clouds that obscure the sun and the moon. From ancient times to the present, immortals and sages have followed one another to dwell there in meditation, and there is now a deva temple that still observes the traditional rites. In the past, the Tathāgata also resided here and preached the profound Dharma extensively for devas and humans. To the south of the great city is a stūpa where the Tathāgata preached the Dharma for three months. Beside it are the sites of the seats and walking paths of the three past Buddhas. Not far to the west of the walking paths of the three Buddhas is a stūpa; this is the birthplace of the bhikṣu Śrotaviṃśatikoṭi (室縷多頻設底拘胝) (in Chinese, "Heard of Two Hundred Koṭis" [聞二百億]; the old translation "Koṭikarṇa" [億耳, "Koṭi-Ear"] is wrong). In the past, there was a wealthy and noble elder in this city who had a child late in life. to the one who then brought him the news he at once gave two hundred koṭis of gold coins, and thus he named his son Śrotaviṃśatikoṭi (He who heard of two hundred koṭis). By the time he reached adulthood, he had never once walked upon the ground, and thus the hair on the soles of his feet was over a foot long, lustrous, fine, and soft, with a color like yellow gold. Cherishing this child, his parents provided him with every kind of luxury; from his residence all the way to the Snow Mountains, post-stations were linked together and servants lined the roads, so that whenever a rare medicine was required, the word was passed along and the item delivered in succession, arriving in no time at all—such was the extent of his great wealth. The World-Honored One, knowing that his roots of goodness were about to sprout, commanded Maudgalyāyana (沒特伽羅子) to go and convert him. Upon arriving at his gate, he found no way to announce himself. The elder’s family worshipped the Sun Deity, and every morning they would face east to bow. At that time, the Venerable One used his supernatural powers to descend from the solar disc and stand before them. The elder’s son, suspecting he was the Sun Deity, offered him fragrant rice; the Venerable One then returned, and the aroma of the rice filled the entire city of Rājagṛha (王舍城). At that time, King Bimbisāra (頻毘娑羅王) was astonished by the extraordinary fragrance and ordered a messenger to investigate; it was discovered that Maudgalyāyana of the Bamboo Grove Monastery (竹林精舍) had brought the rice from the elder's house, and thus, learning that the elder's son possessed such a wonder, the king summoned him. The elder accepted the command, but pondered how to travel safely. To travel by boat and ply the oars carried the danger of wind and waves; to ride in a carriage or on an elephant brought the fear of stumbling or falling. Thereupon, from his residence to the city of Rājagṛha, he excavated a canal for transport and filled it with mustard seeds, so that the boat could rest securely and be towed along by a long rope. Upon arriving at the city of Rājagṛha, he first paid homage to the World-Honored One. The World-Honored One said to him, "King Bimbisāra has ordered a messenger to summon you for no other reason than to see the hair on the soles of your feet. If the king wishes to see them, you should sit in the cross-legged position. To extend your feet toward the king is a capital offense according to the laws of the country." The elder's son accepted this instruction and went to the court, where he was led in to have an audience. When the king wished to see the hair, he sat in the cross-legged position; the king praised his courtesy and came to cherish him deeply. Once he was able to return, he went back to the place of the Buddha. At that time, the Tathāgata (如來) preached the Dharma and offered him instruction; upon hearing it, he was moved to realization and immediately renounced the household life. Thereupon, he practiced with diligent effort, seeking to realize the fruits of enlightenment; he engaged in walking meditation without rest until his feet began to bleed. The World-Honored One said to him, "Good man, when you were at home as a layman, did you know how to play the lute?" He replied, "I did." "If that is so, take this as an analogy. If the strings are too tight, the sound will not be in harmony; if the strings are too loose, the melody will not be refined. Neither too tight nor too loose, the sound is then harmonious. The practitioner of the path is also like this. If one is too urgent, the body becomes exhausted and the mind weary; if one is too lax, the passions expand and the will becomes dissipated." Having received the Buddha's instruction, he followed it faithfully, and before long, he attained the realization of the fruit.

zh: 大城側，臨殑伽河，有伊爛拏山，含吐烟霞，蔽虧日月，古今仙聖繼踵棲神，今有天祠尚遵遺則。在昔如來亦嘗居此，為諸天、人廣說妙法。
en_current: Beside the great city, overlooking the Ganges (殑伽河) River, is Mount Īraṇa (伊爛拏山), which breathes forth mists and clouds that obscure the sun and moon. From ancient times to the present, immortals and sages have followed one another to dwell here in meditation, and there is now a deva temple that still observes the traditional rites. In the past, the Tathāgata also resided here, extensively expounding the wonderful Dharma for the sake of devas and humans.

zh: 國西界殑伽河南，至小孤山，重巘嶜崟，昔佛於此三月安居，降薄句羅藥叉。山東南巖下大石上，有佛坐跡，入石寸餘，長五尺二寸，廣二尺一寸，其上則建窣堵波焉。次南石上則有佛置捃稚迦（即澡瓶也。舊曰軍持，訛略也）跡，深寸餘，作八出花文。佛坐跡東南不遠，有薄句羅藥叉脚跡，長尺五六寸，廣七八寸，深減二寸。藥叉跡後有石佛坐像，高六七尺。次西不遠有佛經行之處。其山頂上有藥叉故室。次北有佛足跡，長尺有八寸，廣餘六寸，深可半寸，其跡上有窣堵波。如來昔日降伏藥叉，令不殺人食肉，敬受佛戒，後得生天。此西有溫泉六七所，其水極熱。國南界大山林中多諸野象，其形偉大。
en_current: At the western border of the country, south of the Gaṅgā (殑伽河) River, one reaches the Small Isolated Hill (小孤山). Its layered peaks are lofty and precipitous. In the past, the Buddha spent three months of the rainy season retreat here, subduing the yakṣa Bakula (薄句羅). On a large rock below the southeastern cliff of the mountain, there is a trace of where the Buddha sat, which penetrates the stone by more than an inch; it is five feet two inches long and two feet one inch wide, and a stūpa has been built upon it. Next, to the south on the stone, there is a trace where the Buddha placed his kuṇḍikā (捃稚迦) (that is, a water-jar for washing; formerly called *kundī* [軍持], erroneous and abbreviated), which is more than an inch deep and fashioned with an eight-petaled flower design. Not far to the southeast of the Buddha’s sitting trace is the footprint of the yakṣa Bakula, which is one foot five or six inches long, seven or eight inches wide, and slightly less than two inches deep. Behind the yakṣa’s footprint is a stone seated image of the Buddha, six or seven feet high. Not far to the west is a place where the Buddha walked in meditation. On the summit of the mountain is the former dwelling of the yakṣa. Next, to the north, is a footprint of the Buddha, one foot eight inches long, over six inches wide, and about half an inch deep; there is a stūpa above this trace. In the past, the Tathāgata subdued the yakṣa, causing him to stop killing people and eating meat, and to respectfully receive the Buddha’s precepts, after which he was reborn in the heavens. To the west of this are six or seven hot springs, the water of which is extremely hot. In the great mountain forests at the southern border of the country, there are many wild elephants, which are immense in size.

zh: 從此順殑伽河南岸東行三百餘里，至瞻波國（中印度境）。瞻波國，周四千餘里。國大都城北背殑伽河，周四十餘里。土地墊濕，稼穡滋盛。氣序溫暑，風俗淳質。伽藍數十所，多有傾毀，僧徒二百餘人，習小乘教。天祠二十餘所，異道雜居。都城壘甎，其高數丈，基址崇峻，却敵高險。在昔劫初，人物伊始，野居穴處，未知宮室。後有天女，降迹人中，遊殑伽河，濯流自媚，感靈有娠，生四子焉。分贍部洲，各擅區宇，建都築邑，封畺畫界，此則一子之國都，贍部洲諸城之始也。
en_current: From here, traveling east for more than three hundred li along the southern bank of the Ganges (Gaṅgā) River, one arrives at the country of Campā (瞻波國) (within the borders of Central India). The country of Campā is more than four thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country has the Ganges River to its north and is more than forty li in circuit. The land is low and damp, and the crops are lush and abundant. The climate is warm and hot, and the customs are simple and honest. There are several dozen saṃghārāmas, most of which are dilapidated, with more than two hundred monks who study the teachings of the Hīnayāna. There are more than twenty deva temples, where followers of various heterodox paths live together. The walls of the capital city are built of brick, several chang high, with lofty and steep foundations and high, precipitous battlements. In the beginning of the kalpa, when human beings first appeared, they lived in the wild and dwelt in caves, not yet knowing of palaces or houses. Later, a celestial maiden descended among humans and, while wandering by the Ganges and bathing in its currents to please herself, she was spiritually moved and became pregnant, eventually giving birth to four sons. They divided Jambudvīpa among themselves, each ruling over a region, building capitals and constructing towns, and marking out boundaries and borders. This city was the capital of one of those sons, and it was the beginning of all the cities in Jambudvīpa.

zh: 城東百四五十里，殑伽河南，水環孤嶼，崖巘崇峻，上有天祠，神多靈感。鑿崖為室，引流成沼，花林奇樹，巨石危峯，仁智所居，觀者忘返。國南境山林中，野象猛獸群遊千數。
en_current: One hundred forty or fifty li to the east of the city, south of the Ganges (gaṅgā), water surrounds a solitary islet with lofty and precipitous cliffs; atop it stands a deva temple where the deity manifests many miracles. Chambers have been carved into the cliffs and water channeled to form ponds; with its flowery groves, exotic trees, massive rocks, and perilous peaks, it is an abode for the benevolent and wise, so beautiful that visitors forget to return. In the mountains and forests of the country's southern border, wild elephants and fierce beasts roam in herds numbering in the thousands.

zh: 自此東行四百餘里，至羯朱嗢祇羅國（彼俗或謂羯蠅揭羅國。中印度境）。羯朱嗢祇羅國，周二千餘里。土地泉濕，稼穡豐盛，氣序溫，風俗順。敦尚高才，崇貴學藝。伽藍六七所，僧徒三百餘人。天祠十所，異道雜居。自數百年，王族絕嗣，役屬隣國，所以城郭丘墟，多居村邑。故戒日王遊東印度，於此築宮，理諸國務，至則葺茅為宇，去則縱火焚燒。國南境多野象。
en_current: Traveling east from here for more than four hundred li, one reaches the country of Kajaṅgala (羯朱嗢祇羅國) (the local people sometimes call it the country of Kayaṅghara [羯蠅揭羅國]; it is within the borders of Central India). The country of Kajaṅgala is more than two thousand li in circuit. The land is moist and marshy, the crops are abundant, the climate is temperate, and the customs are agreeable. The people value high talent and esteem learning and the arts. There are six or seven saṃghārāmas with more than three hundred monks. There are ten deva temples, where followers of various heterodox paths live together. For several hundred years, the royal line has been extinct and the country has been subject to neighboring states; for this reason, the walled cities are in ruins, and the people mostly dwell in villages and towns. Therefore, when King Śīlāditya (戒日王) traveled to East India, he built a palace here to manage the affairs of the various states; when he arrived, he thatched a building with grass, and when he departed, he set fire to it. In the southern borders of the country, there are many wild elephants.

zh: 北境去殑伽河不遠，有大高臺，積壘甎石，而以建焉，基址廣峙，刻雕奇製，周其方面鏤眾聖像，佛及天形區別而作。
en_current: In the northern border, not far from the Ganges (殑伽河; gaṅgā) River, there is a large high terrace built of piled bricks and stones. Its foundation is broad and lofty, featuring exquisite carvings, and all around its sides are engraved images of various holy beings, with the forms of the Buddha and the devas distinctly rendered.

zh: 自此東渡殑伽河，行六百餘里，至奔那伐彈那國（中印度境）。奔那伐彈那國，周四千餘里。國大都城周三十餘里。居人殷盛，池館花林往往相間。土地卑濕，稼穡滋茂。般核娑菓既多且貴，其菓大如冬瓜，熟則黃赤，剖之中有數十小菓，大如鶴卵，又更破之，其汁黃赤，其味甘美。或在樹枝，如眾菓之結實，或在樹根，若伏苓之在土。氣序調暢，風俗好學。伽藍二十餘所，僧徒三千餘人，大小二乘，兼功綜習。天祠百所，異道雜居，露形尼乾寔繁其黨。
en_current: From here, crossing the Gaṅgā (殑伽河) to the east and traveling over six hundred li, one arrives at the country of Puṇḍravardhana (奔那伐彈那國) (within the territory of Central India). The country of Puṇḍravardhana is over four thousand li in circuit. The capital city is more than thirty li in circuit. The inhabitants are numerous and prosperous, and ponds, pavilions, and flower groves are interspersed throughout. The land is low and damp, and the crops are lush and abundant. The *panasa* (般核娑) fruit is both plentiful and highly valued; the fruit is as large as a winter melon, and when ripe, it turns yellowish-red. When sliced open, it contains several dozen smaller fruits as large as crane eggs, and when these are further broken, they yield a yellowish-red juice with a sweet and delicious taste. Some grow on the tree branches like the fruits of other trees, while others grow from the roots, like *fuling* (伏苓) in the soil. The climate is temperate and pleasant, and the customs favor learning. There are more than twenty saṃghārāmas (伽藍) with over three thousand monks, who study both the Great and Lesser Vehicles with equal diligence. There are one hundred deva temples, where followers of various heterodox sects dwell together, and the Nirgrantha (尼乾) ascetics, who go naked, are particularly numerous among their groups.

zh: 城西二十餘里有跋始婆僧伽藍。庭宇顯敞，臺閣崇高。僧徒七百餘人，並學大乘教法，東印度境碩學名僧多在於此。其側不遠有窣堵波，無憂王之所建也。昔者如來三月在此為諸天、人說法之處，或至齋日，時燭光明。其側則有四佛坐及經行遺跡之所。去此不遠復有精舍，中作觀自在菩薩像，神鑒無隱，靈應有徵，遠近之人，絕粒祈請。
en_current: More than twenty li to the west of the city is the Vāśibhā Monastery (跋始婆僧伽藍). Its courtyards and buildings are spacious and open, and its terraces and pavilions are lofty. There are more than seven hundred monks, all of whom study the Mahayana teachings; most of the eminent scholars and renowned monks of East India reside here. Not far to its side is a stupa (窣堵波) built by King Aśoka. This is the place where, in the past, the Tathāgata spent three months preaching the Dharma for the devas and humans; on fast days, it sometimes emits a brilliant light. To its side are the sites of the sitting and walking meditation paths of the four Buddhas. Not far from here is another shrine (精舍), in which is an image of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara. Its spiritual insight is all-revealing and its divine responses are manifest, so that people from far and near fast and pray before it.

zh: 自此東行九百餘里，渡大河，至迦摩縷波國（東印度境）。迦摩縷波國，周萬餘里。國大都城周三十餘里。土地泉濕，稼穡時播。般核娑菓、那羅雞羅菓，其樹雖多，彌復珍貴。河流湖陂，交帶城邑。氣序和暢，風俗淳質。人形卑小，容貌釐黑。語言少異中印度。性甚獷暴，志存強學。宗事天神，不信佛法。故自佛興以迄于今，尚未建立伽藍，招集僧侶。其有淨信之徒，但竊念而已。天祠數百，異道數萬。今王本那羅延天之祚胤，婆羅門之種也，字婆塞羯羅伐摩（唐言日胄），號拘摩羅（唐言童子）。自據畺土，奕葉君臨，逮於今王，歷千世矣。君上好學，眾庶從化，遠方高才，慕義客遊，雖不淳信佛法，然敬高學沙門。初，聞有至那國沙門在摩揭陀那爛陀僧伽藍，自遠方來，學佛深法，殷勤往復者再三，未從來命。時尸羅跋陀羅論師曰：「欲報佛恩，當弘正法，子其行矣，勿憚遠涉。拘摩羅王世宗外道，今請沙門，斯善事也，因茲改轍，福利弘遠。子昔起廣大心，發弘誓，願孤遊異域，遺身求法，普濟含靈，豈徒鄉國？宜忘得喪，勿拘榮辱，宣揚聖教，開導群迷，先物後身，忘名弘法。」於是辭不獲免，遂與使偕行，而會見焉。拘摩羅王曰：「雖則不才，常慕高學，聞名雅尚，敢事延請。」曰：「寡能褊智，猥蒙流聽。」拘摩羅王曰：「善哉！慕法好學，顧身若浮，踰越重險，遠遊異域。斯則王化所由，國風尚學。今印度諸國多有歌頌摩訶至那國《秦王破陣樂》者，聞之久矣，豈大德之鄉國耶？」曰：「然，此歌者，美我君之德也。」拘摩羅王曰：「不意大德是此國人，常慕風化，東望已久，山川道阻，無由自致。」曰：「我大君聖德遠洽，仁化遐被，殊俗異域拜闕稱臣者眾矣。」拘摩羅王曰：「覆載若斯，心冀朝貢。今戒日王在羯朱嗢祇羅國，將設大施，崇樹福慧，五印度沙門、婆羅門有學業者，莫不召集。今遣使來請，願與同行。」於是遂往焉。此國東山阜連接，無大國都，境接西南夷，故其人類蠻獠矣。詳問土俗，可兩月行，入蜀西南之境，然山川險阻，嶂氣氛沴，毒蛇毒草，為害滋甚。國之東南野象群暴，故此國中象軍特盛。
en_current: From here, traveling east for over nine hundred li and crossing a great river, one reaches the country of Kāmarūpa (迦摩縷波國) (in the territory of East India). The country of Kāmarūpa is over ten thousand li in circuit. The capital city is over thirty li in circuit. The land is low and moist, and crops are sown at the proper seasons. Although there are many *panasa* (般核娑 - jackfruit) and *nārikela* (那羅雞羅 - coconut) trees, they are considered very precious. Rivers, lakes, and ponds encircle the cities and towns. The climate is mild and pleasant, and the customs are simple and honest. The people are short in stature and dark in complexion. Their language differs slightly from that of Central India. Their nature is very fierce and impetuous, but they are determined to study diligently. They revere and serve the heavenly gods and do not believe in the Buddha-dharma. Therefore, from the time the Buddha appeared until the present, no monasteries have been built to gather monks. Those who have pure faith only pay homage in secret. There are several hundred deva temples and tens of thousands of non-Buddhists. The reigning king is a descendant of the god Nārāyaṇa and belongs to the Brahman caste; his name is Bhāskaravarman (婆塞羯羅伐摩) (in the language of Tang, "Sun-Armor"), and his title is Kumāra (拘摩羅) (in the language of Tang, "Youth"). Since he first occupied this territory, his family has ruled for a thousand generations down to the present king. The king is fond of learning, and the common people follow his example; men of high talent from distant lands, admiring his righteousness, come to travel as his guests. Although he does not sincerely believe in the Buddha-dharma, he respects learned śramaṇas. Previously, having heard that a śramaṇa from the country of Cīna (至那國) was at the Nālandā (那爛陀) Monastery in Magadha, having come from afar to study the profound Dharma of the Buddha, the king sent cordial invitations back and forth three times, but the monk had not yet complied with the request. At that time, the Master of Treatises Śīlabhadra (尸羅跋陀羅) said, "If you wish to repay the Buddha’s kindness, you must propagate the True Dharma. You should go; do not fear the long journey. The family of King Kumāra (拘摩羅王) has followed non-Buddhist paths for generations, and his invitation to a śramaṇa is a virtuous deed. If he changes his course because of this, the benefits will be vast and far-reaching. You previously aroused a great mind and made a grand vow, wishing to travel alone to foreign lands, casting aside your body to seek the Dharma and universally save all sentient beings—how could this be limited to your own country? You should forget about gain and loss, disregard honor and disgrace, propagate the holy teachings, enlighten the deluded, put others before yourself, and forget personal fame to spread the Dharma."  Thereupon, being unable to decline, he accompanied the envoy and went to meet him. King Kumāra said, "Although I am without talent, I have always admired those of high learning. Having heard of your fame and noble character, I ventured to invite you." He replied, "I am of little ability and narrow wisdom, yet I have undeservedly received your attention."  King Kumāra said, "Excellent! You admire the Dharma and love learning, regarding your own body as light as a feather, crossing heavy dangers to travel far to foreign lands. This is the source of royal transformation and the reason why the customs of your country value learning. Now, in all the countries of India, there are many who sing the 'Music of the King of Qin Breaking the Battle Lines' (秦王破陣樂) of the country of Mahācīna (摩訶至那國); I have heard it for a long time. Is this not the country of the Great Virtuous One?" He replied, "Indeed, this song praises the virtues of my sovereign."  King Kumāra said, "I did not realize that you, Great Virtuous One, were a man of this country. I have always admired its refined culture and have long looked toward the East, but as the mountains and rivers block the way, I have had no means to go there myself." I replied, "The sacred virtues of our great monarch spread far and wide, and his benevolent influence reaches distant lands; those from foreign regions with different customs who come to the imperial palace to pay homage and declare themselves subjects are numerous indeed." King Kumāra said, "Since his grace covers all like heaven and earth, I have long hoped to send tribute. Now King Śīlāditya (戒日王) is in the country of Kajuṅghira (羯朱嗢祇羅國), where he is about to hold a great almsgiving to cultivate merit and wisdom; all the Śramaṇas and Brahmins of the five Indias who possess learning have been summoned to assemble. He has now sent an envoy to invite me, and I wish for you to travel with me." I therefore went with him.  In the eastern part of this country, mountains and hills are interconnected, and there are no large capital cities; as its borders adjoin the Southwest Yi (西南夷), its people resemble the Man (蠻) and Lao (獠) tribes. I inquired in detail about the local customs and learned that one could reach the southwestern borders of Shu (蜀) in about two months' travel; however, the mountains and rivers are treacherous and obstructed, the mountain mists are noxious, and poisonous snakes and herbs cause great harm. In the southeast of the country, wild elephants roam in violent herds, which is why the elephant corps of this country is particularly numerous.

zh: 東行九百餘里，渡大河，至迦摩縷波國
en_current: Traveling east for over nine hundred li, one crosses a great river and reaches the country of Kāmarūpa (迦摩縷波國).

zh: 從此南行千二三百里，至三摩呾吒國（東印度境）。三摩呾吒國，周三千餘里。濱近大海，地遂卑濕。國大都城周二十餘里。稼穡滋植，花菓繁茂。氣序和，風俗順。人性剛烈，形卑色黑，好學勤勵，邪正兼信。伽藍三十餘所，僧徒二千餘人，並皆遵習上座部學。天祠百所，異道雜居，露形尼乾，其徒甚盛。去城不遠有窣堵波，無憂王之所建也。昔者如來為諸天、人於此七日說深妙法。傍有四佛坐及經行遺迹之所。去此不遠，伽藍中有青玉佛像，其高八尺，相好圓備，靈應時効。從此東北大海濱山谷中，有室利差呾羅國。次東南大海隅有迦摩浪迦國。次東有墮羅鉢底國。次東有伊賞那補羅國。次東有摩訶瞻波國，即此云林邑是也。次西南有閻摩那洲國。凡此六國，山川道阻，不入其境，然風俗壤，界聲聞可知。
en_current: From here, traveling south for one thousand two hundred or one thousand three hundred li, one reaches the country of Samataṭa (三摩呾吒國) (in the territory of eastern India). The country of Samataṭa is more than three thousand li in circuit. It borders the great ocean, and the land is low and damp. The great capital city is more than twenty li in circuit. The crops are lush and the flowers and fruits are abundant. The climate is temperate and the customs are harmonious. The people are fierce by nature, short in stature, and dark in complexion; they are diligent in learning and believe in both heterodox and orthodox teachings. There are more than thirty saṃghārāmas with over two thousand monks, all of whom follow the teachings of the Sthavira school. There are one hundred deva temples where followers of various heterodox paths live together, and the naked Nirgrantha ascetics are particularly numerous. Not far from the city is a stūpa built by King Aśoka. In the past, the Tathāgata preached the profound and wonderful Dharma here for seven days for the sake of devas and humans. Nearby are the sites of the four Buddhas' sitting and walking meditation. Not far from this, in a saṃghārāma, there is a green jade Buddha image eight feet high, with all the physical marks perfectly complete, which frequently manifests miraculous responses.  From here, to the northeast, in a valley by the seaside, is the country of Śrīkṣetra (室利差呾羅國). Next, to the southeast, in a corner of the great ocean, is the country of Kamalāṅkā (迦摩浪迦國). Next, to the east, is the country of Dvāravatī (墮羅鉢底國). Next, to the east, is the country of Īśānapura (伊賞那補羅國). Next, to the east, is the country of Mahācampā (摩訶瞻波國), which is what is called Linyi (林邑) here. Next, to the southwest, is the country of Yamanadvīpa (閻摩那洲國). Regarding these six countries, the mountains and rivers make the roads difficult, so I did not enter their borders; however, their customs and territories can be known by hearsay.

zh: 從此東北大海濱山谷中，有室利差呾羅國。
en_current: To the northeast of here, in a valley by the shore of the great sea, is the kingdom of Śrīkṣetra (室利差呾羅國).

zh: 次東南大海隅有迦摩浪迦國。
en_current: Further to the southeast, at a corner of the great sea, is the country of Kāmalaṅkā (迦摩浪迦國).

zh: 次東有墮羅鉢底國。
en_current: Next, to the east, is the country of Dvāravatī (墮羅鉢底國).

zh: 次東有伊賞那補羅國。
en_current: To the east of this is the country of Īśānapura (伊賞那補羅國).

zh: 次東有摩訶瞻波國，即此云林邑是也。
en_current: Further to the east is the country of Mahācampā (摩訶瞻波國), which is what is called Linyi (林邑) here.

zh: 次西南有閻摩那洲國。凡此六國，山川道阻，不入其境，然風俗壤，界聲聞可知。
en_current: To the southwest is the country of Yamanadvīpa (閻摩那洲國). Regarding these six countries, the routes are obstructed by mountains and rivers, and I did not enter their territories; however, their customs, lands, and boundaries are known through report.

zh: 自三摩呾吒國西行九百餘里，至耽摩栗底國（東印度境）。耽摩栗底國，周千四五百里。國大都城周十餘里。濱近海垂，土地卑濕。稼穡時播，花菓茂盛。氣序溫暑，風俗躁烈。人性剛勇，邪正兼信。伽藍十餘所，僧眾千餘人。天祠五十餘所，異道雜居。國濱海隅，水陸交會，奇珍異寶，多聚此國，故其國人大抵殷富。城側窣堵波，無憂王所建也。其傍則有過去四佛坐及經行遺迹之所。
en_current: Traveling west from the country of Samataṭa (三摩呾吒國) for over nine hundred li, one reaches the country of Tāmraliptī (耽摩栗底國) (within the borders of East India). The country of Tāmraliptī is about one thousand four or five hundred li in circuit. The capital city is over ten li in circuit. It is situated near the edge of the sea; the land is low and damp. Crops are sown in their proper seasons, and flowers and fruits are abundant. The climate is warm and hot, and the customs are impetuous and fierce. The people are courageous and brave, and they believe in both heterodox and orthodox teachings. There are more than ten saṃghārāmas and over one thousand monks. There are more than fifty deva temples, where followers of different paths live together. As the country is situated on a sea corner where water and land routes meet, rare and precious treasures are gathered here in abundance, and for this reason, the people of the country are generally wealthy. Beside the city is a stūpa built by King Aśoka. Nearby are the sites of the seats and walking paths of the four past Buddhas.

zh: 自此西北行七百餘里，至羯羅拏蘇伐剌那國（東印度境）。羯羅拏蘇伐剌那國，周四千四五百里。國大都城周二十餘里。居人殷盛，家室富饒。土地下濕，稼穡時播，眾花滋茂，珍菓繁植。氣序調暢，風俗淳和。好尚學藝，邪正兼信。伽藍十餘所，僧徒二千餘人，習學小乘正量部法。天祠五十餘所，異道寔多。別有三伽藍，不食乳酪，遵提婆達多遺訓也。
en_current: From here, traveling northwest for over seven hundred li, one reaches the country of Karṇasuvarṇa (羯羅拏蘇伐剌那國) (in the territory of East India). The country of Karṇasuvarṇa is four thousand four or five hundred li in circuit. The capital city is over twenty li in circuit. The inhabitants are prosperous and the households are wealthy. The land is low and damp; crops are sown in their proper seasons, and various flowers and precious fruits grow in abundance. The climate is temperate and the customs are honest and harmonious. The people value learning and the arts, and they believe in both heterodox and orthodox teachings. There are more than ten monasteries with over two thousand monks, who study the teachings of the Sāmmitīya school of the Hīnayāna. There are more than fifty Deva temples, and the number of non-Buddhists is very large. Separately, there are three monasteries where the monks do not consume milk or cream, following the legacy of Devadatta.

zh: 大城側有絡多未知僧伽藍（唐言赤泥）。庭宇顯敞，臺閣崇峻。國中高才達學、聰敏有聞者，咸集其中，警誡相成，琢磨道德。初，此國未信佛法時，南印度有一外道，腹錮銅鍱，首戴明炬，杖策高步，來入此城，振擊論鼓，求欲談議。或者問曰：「首腹何異？」曰：「吾學藝多能，恐腹拆裂；悲諸愚闇，所以持照。」時經旬日，人無問者，詢訪髦彥，莫有異人。王曰：「合境之內，豈無明哲？客難不酬，為國深恥。宜更營求，訪諸幽隱。」或曰：「大林中有異人，其自稱曰沙門，強學是務，今屏居幽寂，久矣于茲，非夫體法合德，何能若此者乎？」王聞之，躬往請焉。沙門對曰：「我，南印度人也，客遊止此，學業膚淺，恐黜所聞。敢承來旨，不復固辭。論議無負，請建伽藍，招集僧徒，光讚佛法。」王曰：「敬聞，不敢忘德。」沙門受請，往赴論場。外道於是誦其宗致，三萬餘言。其義遠，其文約，苞含名相，網羅視聽。沙門一聞究覽，辭義無謬，以數百言，辯而釋之，因問宗致。外道辭窮理屈，杜口不酬。既折其名，負恥而退。王深敬德，建此伽藍，自時厥後，方弘法教。伽藍側不遠有窣堵波，無憂王所建也，在昔如來於此七日說法開導。其側精舍，過去四佛坐及經行遺迹之所。有數窣堵波，並是如來說法之處，無憂王之所建也。
en_current: Beside the great city is the Raktamṛttikā Monastery (絡多未知僧伽藍) (in Chinese, "Red Clay"). Its courtyards and buildings are spacious and open, and its towers and pavilions are lofty and steep. The highly talented and profoundly learned scholars of the country, as well as those of renowned intelligence, all assemble therein to assist one another through mutual admonition and to cultivate their morality and virtue.  Formerly, before this country believed in the Buddha-dharma, there was a heretic from South India who bound his belly with copper plates, wore a bright torch upon his head, and, leaning on a staff, walked with proud strides into this city, where he struck the drum of debate and sought to engage in discussion. Someone asked him, "Why do you wear a torch on your head and plates on your belly?" He replied, "My learning and skills are so vast that I fear my belly might burst; I pity the ignorance of others, which is why I carry this light."  Ten days passed, and no one came to question him. They inquired among the eminent and wise, but there was no one who could match him. The king said, "Within the borders of this realm, can there be no wise and enlightened men? To leave a guest's challenge unanswered is a deep shame for the country. We should search further and inquire among those living in seclusion."  Someone said, "In the great forest there is an extraordinary man who calls himself a śramaṇa; he is dedicated to arduous study and has lived here in quiet seclusion for a long time. Were he not one who embodies the Dharma and accords with virtue, how could he live like this?"  The king heard this and went in person to invite him. The śramaṇa replied, "I am a man of South India staying here as a traveler; my learning is superficial, and I fear I may fall short of what you have heard. However, I dare to accept your command and will no longer firmly decline. If I am not defeated in the debate, I request that you build a monastery, gather monks together, and glorify and promote the Buddha-dharma." The king said, "I respectfully hear your words and dare not forget your virtue." The śramaṇa accepted the invitation and went to the site of the debate. The non-Buddhist then recited his tenets, totaling more than thirty thousand words. Their meaning was profound and their phrasing concise; they encompassed all names and characteristics, capturing the sight and hearing of the audience. The śramaṇa, having heard them once, comprehended them completely, without error in wording or meaning, and with a few hundred words, he debated and refuted them, then questioned the non-Buddhist on his tenets. The non-Buddhist, his arguments exhausted and his logic defeated, sealed his mouth and could not respond. Having been refuted in his reputation, he retreated in shame. The king deeply respected the śramaṇa’s virtue and built this monastery; from that time thereafter, the Buddha-dharma was widely propagated. Not far from the side of the monastery is a stūpa, which was built by King Aśoka (無憂王); in the past, the Tathāgata stayed here for seven days to preach the Dharma and provide guidance. Beside it is a *vihāra* (精舍), the place where the past four Buddhas left traces of sitting and walking in meditation. There are several stūpas, all of which are places where the Tathāgata preached the Dharma, and they were built by King Aśoka.

zh: 從此西南行七百餘里，至烏荼國（東印度境）。烏荼國，周七千餘里。國大都城周二十餘里。土地膏腴，穀稼茂盛，凡諸菓實，頗大諸國，異草名花，難以稱述。氣序溫暑，風俗獷烈。人貌魁梧，容色釐黮。言辭風調，異中印度。好學不倦，多信佛法，伽藍百餘所，僧徒萬餘人，並皆習學大乘法教。天祠五十所，異道雜居。諸窣堵波凡十餘所，並是如來說法之處，無憂王之所建也。
en_current: Traveling southwest from here for over seven hundred li, one reaches the country of Uḍra (烏荼國) (in the region of East India). The country of Uḍra is over seven thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the kingdom is over twenty li in circuit. The land is rich and fertile, and the crops and grains grow luxuriantly; all kinds of fruits are much larger than in other countries, and the exotic grasses and famous flowers are difficult to describe. The climate is warm and hot, and the customs are fierce and impetuous. The people are tall and robust in appearance, and their complexions are dark. Their speech and mannerisms differ from those of Central India. They are diligent in learning and mostly believe in the Buddhadharma; there are more than one hundred saṃghārāmas and over ten thousand monks, all of whom study the teachings of the Mahāyāna. There are fifty deva temples, where followers of different paths live together. There are more than ten stūpas in total, all of which are places where the Tathāgata preached the Dharma, and were built by King Aśoka.

zh: 國西南境大山中，有補澁波祇釐僧伽藍，其石窣堵波極多靈異，或至齋日，時燭光明。故諸淨信，遠近咸會，持妙花蓋，競修供養。承露盤下，覆鉢勢上，以花蓋笴，置之便住，若礠石之吸針也。
en_current: In the great mountains on the southwestern border of the kingdom is the Puṣpagiri (補澁波祇釐) monastery. Its stone stūpa possesses many spiritual anomalies; sometimes, on fast days, it emits a bright light. Therefore, the pure-hearted faithful, from both near and far, all gather there, holding exquisite flower canopies and vying to perform offerings. Below the dew-receiving basin and above the inverted-bowl structure, if one places the handle of a flower canopy, it remains fixed there as if a magnet were attracting a needle.

zh: 此西北山伽藍中有窣堵波，所異同前。此二窣堵波者，神鬼所建，靈奇若斯。
en_current: In the monastery in the mountains to the northwest, there is a stūpa whose miraculous properties are the same as the former. These two stūpas were built by spirits and deities, and their spiritual wonders are of such a nature.

zh: 國東南境臨大海濱，有折利呾羅城（唐言發行）。周二十餘里，入海商人、遠方旅客，往來中止之路也。其城堅峻，多諸奇寶。城外鱗次有五伽藍，臺閣崇高，尊像工麗。南去僧伽羅國二萬餘里，靜夜遙望，見彼國佛牙窣堵波上寶珠光明。離然如明炬之懸燭也。
en_current: On the southeastern border of the country, facing the coast of the great ocean, is the city of Caritra (折利呾羅城; translated in Chinese as "Departure"). It is over twenty *li* in circuit and serves as a thoroughfare and stopping place for seafaring merchants and travelers from distant lands. The city is solid and steep, and it contains many rare treasures. Outside the city, five monasteries stand in a row; their terraces and pavilions are lofty, and the sacred images are exquisitely crafted. To the south, the country of Siṃhala (僧伽羅國) is over twenty thousand *li* away; gazing into the distance on a quiet night, one can see the light of the precious pearl atop the Buddha-tooth stūpa of that land, shining clearly like a torch suspended in the air.

zh: 自此西南大林中行千二百餘里，至恭御陀國（東印度境）。恭御陀國，周千餘里。國大都城周二十餘里。濱近海隅，山阜隱軫，土地墊濕，稼穡時播。氣序溫暑，風俗勇烈。其形偉，其貌黑。粗有禮義，不甚欺詐。至於文字，同中印度，語言風調，頗有異焉。崇敬外道，不信佛法。天祠百餘所，異道萬餘人。國境之內，數十小城，接山嶺，據海交，城既堅峻，兵又敢勇，威雄隣境，遂無強敵。國臨海濱，多有奇寶，螺貝珠璣，斯為貨用。出大青象，超乘致遠。
en_current: From here, traveling southwest through a great forest for more than one thousand two hundred li, one reaches the country of Koṅgoda (恭御陀國) (in the region of East India). The country of Koṅgoda is more than one thousand li in circuit. The capital city is more than twenty li in circuit. It borders the seashore; the mountains and hills are rugged and undulating, the land is low and damp, and crops are sown in their proper seasons. The climate is warm and hot, and the customs of the people are bold and fierce. Their stature is large, and their complexion is black. They possess a rough sense of propriety and righteousness, and are not very deceitful. As for their writing, it is the same as that of Central India, but their language and manner of speech differ considerably. They revere non-Buddhist sects and do not believe in the Buddha-dharma. There are more than one hundred Deva temples and over ten thousand followers of non-Buddhist paths. Within the borders of the country, there are several dozen small towns situated near mountain ranges and occupying the junctions of sea routes. The city walls are strong and steep, and the soldiers are brave and daring; their power dominates the neighboring lands, and thus they have no formidable enemies. The country borders the sea, and there are many rare treasures; conch shells, pearls, and precious stones are used as currency. They produce large dark-colored elephants, which are capable of traveling long distances when ridden.

zh: 從此西南入大荒野，深林巨木，干霄蔽日，行千四五百里，至羯𩜁（力甑反）伽國（南印度境）。羯𩜁伽國，周五千餘里。國大都城周二十餘里。稼穡時播，花果具繁，林藪聯綿，動數百里。出青野象，隣國所奇。氣序暑熱，風俗躁暴，性多狷獷，志存信義。言語輕捷，音調質正，辭旨風則，頗與中印度異焉。少信正法，多遵外道，伽藍十餘所，僧徒五百餘人，習學大乘上座部法。天祠百餘所，異道甚眾，多是尼乾之徒也。羯𩜁伽國在昔之時，民俗殷盛，肩摩轂擊，舉袂成帷。有五通仙棲巖養素，人或陵觸，退失神通，以惡呪術殘害國人，少長無遺，賢愚俱喪。人煙斷絕，多歷年所，頗漸遷居，猶未充實，故今此國人戶尚少。城南不遠有窣堵波，高百餘尺，無憂王之所建也。傍有過去四佛坐及經行遺迹之所。
en_current: From here, traveling southwest into a vast wilderness with deep forests and giant trees that reached the sky and obscured the sun, one proceeds for one thousand four or five hundred *li* to the country of Kaliṅga (羯𩜁伽國) (𩜁 is pronounced by the *fanqie* 力甑) (in the region of South India). The country of Kaliṅga is more than five thousand *li* in circuit. The capital city is more than twenty *li* in circuit. Crops are sown in their proper seasons, and flowers and fruits are abundant; forests and marshes stretch continuously for hundreds of *li*. It produces dark wild elephants, which are prized by neighboring countries. The climate is hot, and the customs are impetuous and violent; the people are by nature impatient and fierce, yet they value faith and righteousness. Their speech is rapid and light, their tone is simple and direct, and their diction and style are quite different from those of Central India. Few believe in the true Dharma, and most follow non-Buddhist paths. There are more than ten monasteries with over five hundred monks, who study the teachings of the Mahāyāna Sthavira school. There are more than one hundred *deva* temples, and the number of heterodox practitioners is very great, most of whom are followers of the Nirgrantha. In former times, the country of Kaliṅga was prosperous and densely populated, with shoulders rubbing and wheel hubs clashing, and the raising of sleeves would form a curtain. A sage possessing the five supernatural powers was dwelling in the rocks and cultivating purity; because people insulted and provoked him, he lost his supernatural powers and used evil spells to slaughter the people of the country, leaving no one, young or old, and destroying both the wise and the foolish. Human habitation was cut off for many years. Gradually, people have moved back, but it is still not fully populated; therefore, the number of households in this country is currently small. Not far south of the city is a *stūpa* more than one hundred feet high, built by King Aśoka. Beside it are the sites of the traces of the sitting and walking meditation of the four past Buddhas.

zh: 國境北垂，大山嶺上有石窣堵波，高百餘尺，是劫初時人壽無量歲，有獨覺於此入寂滅焉。
en_current: On the northern frontier of the country, atop the great mountain ridge, there is a stone stupa over a hundred feet high. It is the place where, at the beginning of the kalpa when the human lifespan was immeasurable, a Pratyekabuddha entered into extinction.

zh: 自此西北山林中行千八百餘里，至憍薩羅國（中印度境）。憍薩羅國，周六千餘里，山嶺周境，林藪連接。國大都城周四十餘里。土壤膏腴，地利滋盛。邑里相望，人戶殷實。其形偉，其色黑。風俗剛猛，人性勇烈。邪正兼信，學藝高明。王，剎帝利也。崇敬佛法，仁慈深遠。伽藍百餘所，僧徒減萬人，並皆習學大乘法教。天祠七十餘所，異道雜居。城南不遠有故伽藍，傍有窣堵波，無憂王之所建也。昔者，如來曾於此處現大神通，摧伏外道。後龍猛菩薩止此伽藍，時此國王號娑多婆訶（唐言引正）。珍敬龍猛，周衛門廬。時提婆菩薩自執師子國來求論義，謂門者曰：「幸為通謁。」時門者遂為白。龍猛雅知其名，盛滿鉢水，命弟子曰：「汝持是水，示彼提婆。」提婆見水，默而投針。弟子持鉢，懷疑而返。龍猛曰：「彼何辭乎？」對曰：「默無所說，但投針於水而已。」龍猛曰：「智矣哉，若人也！知幾其神，察微亞聖，盛德若此，宜速命入。」對曰：「何謂也？無言妙辯，斯之是歟？」曰：「夫水也者，隨器方圓，逐物清濁，彌漫無間，澄湛莫測。滿而示之，比我學之智周也；彼乃投針，遂窮其極。此非常人，宜速召進。」而龍猛風範懍然肅物，言談者皆伏抑首。提婆素挹風徽，久希請益，方欲受業，先騁機神，雅懼威嚴，昇堂僻坐，談玄永日，辭義清高。龍猛曰：「後學冠世，妙辯光前，我惟衰耄，遇斯俊彥，誠乃寫瓶有寄，傳燈不絕，法教弘揚，伊人是賴。幸能前席，雅談玄奧。」提婆聞命，心獨自負，將開義府，先遊辯囿，提振辭端，仰視質義。忽覩威顏，忘言杜口，避坐引責，遂請受業。龍猛曰：「復坐，今將授子至真妙理，法王誠教。」提婆五體投地，一心歸命，曰：「而今而後，敢聞命矣。」龍猛菩薩善閑藥術，飡餌養生，壽年數百，志貌不衰。引正王既得妙藥，壽亦數百。王有稚子，謂其母曰：「如我何時得嗣王位？」母曰：「以今觀之，未有期也。父王年壽已數百歲，子孫老終者蓋亦多矣。斯皆龍猛福力所加，藥術所致。菩薩寂滅，王必殂落。夫龍猛菩薩智慧弘遠，慈悲深厚，周給群有，身命若遺。汝宜往彼，試從乞頭，若遂此志，當果所願。」王子恭承母命，來至伽藍，門者敬懼，故得入焉。時龍猛菩薩方讚誦經行，忽見王子，佇而謂曰：「今夕何因，降跡僧坊，若危若懼，疾驅而至？」對曰：「我承慈母餘論，語及行捨之士，以為含生寶命，經語格言，未有輕捨報身，施諸求欲。我慈母曰：『不然。十方善逝，三世如來，在昔發心，逮乎證果，勤求佛道，修習戒忍。或投身𩚅獸，或割肌救鴿，月光王施婆羅門頭，慈力王飲餓藥叉血，諸若此類，羌難備舉。求之先覺，何代無人？』今龍猛菩薩篤斯高志，我有所求，人頭為用，招募累歲，未之有捨。欲行暴劫殺，則罪累尤多，虐害無辜，穢德彰顯。惟菩薩修習聖道，遠期佛果，慈霑有識，惠及無邊，輕生若浮，賤身如朽，不違本願，垂允所求！」龍猛曰：「俞，誠哉是言也！我求佛聖果，我學佛能捨，是身如響，是身如泡，流轉四生，去來六趣，宿契弘誓，不違物欲。然王子！有一不可者，其將若何？我身既終，汝父亦喪，顧斯為意，誰能濟之？」龍猛俳佪顧視，求所絕命，以乾茅葉自刎其頸，若利劍斷割，身首異處。王子見已，驚奔而去。門者上白，具陳始末，王聞哀感，果亦命終。
en_current: From here, traveling northwest through mountains and forests for over 1,800 li, one reaches the country of Kosala (憍薩羅國) (in the region of Central India). The country of Kosala is over 6,000 li in circumference, with mountain ranges encircling its borders and forests and marshes connected throughout. The capital city of the country is over 40 li in circumference. The soil is rich and fertile, and the land is highly productive. Villages and hamlets look out upon one another, and the households are prosperous and substantial. The people are large in stature and dark in complexion. Their customs are fierce and impetuous, and their nature is brave and violent. They believe in both heterodox and orthodox teachings, and they are highly skilled in the arts. The king is a Kṣatriya. He reveres the Buddha-Dharma and is deeply compassionate and far-reaching in his benevolence. There are over one hundred saṃghārāmas, and the number of monks is just under ten thousand; all of them study the teachings of the Mahāyāna. There are over seventy Deva temples, where followers of different paths live together. Not far to the south of the city is an old saṃghārāma, and beside it is a stūpa built by King Aśoka (無憂王). In the past, the Tathāgata once manifested great supernatural powers at this place to subdue non-Buddhists. Later, the Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna (龍猛菩薩) resided in this saṃghārāma. At that time, the king of this country was named Sātavāhana (娑多婆訶) (in Chinese, "Leading the Righteous"). He cherished and respected Nāgārjuna, and he guarded the gates of his residence. At that time, the Bodhisattva Deva (提婆菩薩) came from the country of Siṃhala (執師子國) to seek a debate, and he said to the gatekeeper, "I would be grateful if you would announce my visit." The gatekeeper then went to report this. Nāgārjuna, already well aware of his reputation, filled a bowl to the brim with water and instructed his disciple, saying, "Take this water and show it to that Deva." When Deva saw the water, he silently dropped a needle into it. The disciple took the bowl and returned, feeling puzzled. Nāgārjuna asked, "What did he say?" The disciple replied, "He said nothing, but merely dropped a needle into the water." Nāgārjuna said, "How wise he is, this man! To know the subtle is divine; to perceive the minute is to be second only to a sage. With such great virtue, he should be invited in immediately." The disciple asked, "What does this mean? Is this what you call the marvelous eloquence of silence?" Nāgārjuna said, "Water takes the shape of its container, whether square or round; it adapts to the purity or turbidity of its surroundings; it permeates everywhere without gaps, and its clarity is unfathomable. I showed him the bowl filled to the brim to signify that my learning is complete; he dropped a needle into it, thereby exhausting its depths. This is no ordinary person; he should be summoned at once." Nāgārjuna’s demeanor was awe-inspiring and commanded respect; all who spoke with him would bow their heads in submission. Deva had long admired his reputation and had long hoped to request instruction. Just as he was about to become a student, he first wished to display his own keen intellect, yet he was also intimidated by Nāgārjuna’s majesty. He ascended the hall, sat to one side, and they discussed the profound mysteries all day long, their discourse clear and lofty. Nāgārjuna said, "Your scholarship surpasses the world and your brilliant eloquence outshines your predecessors. I am but a feeble old man, and meeting such a talented youth truly allows me to pour the contents of my vessel into another and keep the lamp of transmission burning without end; the propagation of the Dharma depends on such a person. I hope you will move to the front seat so that we may discuss the profound mysteries." Upon hearing this command, Deva, who had been confident in his own mind, prepared to open the storehouse of his arguments and first roam the garden of debate. He raised his points and looked up to challenge the meaning, but suddenly catching sight of Nāgārjuna’s majestic countenance, he forgot his words and fell silent. He moved his seat back, acknowledged his fault, and requested to become his student. Nāgārjuna said, "Sit down again. I shall now bestow upon you the most perfect and wonderful truth, the authentic teaching of the Dharma King." Deva prostrated himself, his five limbs touching the ground, and with a single mind surrendered his life, saying, "From this moment on, I dare to follow your instructions." Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva was well-versed in the arts of medicine; by consuming elixirs to nourish his life, he lived for several hundred years, his spirit and appearance showing no signs of decline. The king, Sātavāhana (引正王), having obtained the wonderful medicine, also lived for several hundred years. The king had a young son who said to his mother, "At this rate, when will I ever be able to succeed to the throne?" His mother replied, "Judging by the present situation, there is no prospect. Your father the king has already lived for several hundred years, and many of his descendants have already grown old and died. This is all due to the power of Nāgārjuna’s merit and the efficacy of his medical arts. If the Bodhisattva were to pass away, the king would surely perish. Now, Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva possesses vast wisdom and profound compassion; he provides for all living beings and regards his own life as something to be cast aside. You should go to him and try to beg for his head. If you can fulfill this intention, your wish will be granted." The prince respectfully obeyed his mother’s command and came to the monastery; the gatekeepers were awestruck and fearful, so he was able to enter. At that time, Nāgārjuna Bodhisattva was chanting and walking in meditation. Suddenly seeing the prince, he stopped and asked, "For what reason have you come to the monastery this evening, appearing so anxious and fearful, and rushing here in such haste?" The prince replied, "I have received the words of my compassionate mother, which touched upon those who practice the virtue of giving. I had thought that for all living beings, life is a precious treasure, and that in the words and maxims of the scriptures, there has never been anyone who lightly cast aside their physical body to bestow it upon those who seek it. But my compassionate mother said: 'It is not so. The Sugatas of the ten directions and the Tathāgatas of the three ages, from the time they first resolved their minds until they attained the fruit of enlightenment, diligently sought the Buddha-way and practiced the precepts and forbearance. Some threw their bodies to feed hungry beasts, some cut their flesh to save a dove; King Candraprabha gave his head to a Brahmin, and King Maitrībala gave his blood to satisfy hungry Yakṣas; examples such as these are truly difficult to enumerate fully. In seeking the sages of the past, what age has been without such people?' Now, Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna (龍猛菩薩) is firm in his noble ambitions. I have a request for a human head to use, but though I have sought one for many years, no one has yet offered theirs. If I were to commit a violent robbery and murder, the burden of my sins would be all the greater; to cruelly harm the innocent would make my defiled virtue manifest. Only you, Bodhisattva, who practice the holy path and look toward the distant fruit of Buddhahood, whose compassion moistens all sentient beings and whose kindness reaches the boundless, treat life as lightly as a floating bubble and hold your body as cheaply as rotten wood. Do not violate your original vow, but grant what I request!" Nāgārjuna said: "Yes, these words are indeed true! I seek the holy fruit of Buddhahood and I learn from the Buddha the ability to renounce all. This body is like an echo, this body is like a bubble; it circulates through the four types of birth and comes and goes through the six realms. Bound by a long-standing great vow, I will not oppose the desires of living beings. However, Prince, there is one thing that is not possible; what shall be done about it? Once my body is finished, your father will also perish. Considering this, who could save him?" Nāgārjuna paced about and looked around, seeking a way to end his life. He cut his own throat with a blade of dry cogon grass as if with a sharp sword, and his head was severed from his body. Seeing this, the prince was terrified and fled. The gatekeeper went up and reported the matter, detailing the beginning and the end; upon hearing this, the king was overcome with grief and, as a result, he also passed away.

zh: 國西南三百餘里至跋邏末羅耆釐山（唐言黑蜂）。岌然特起，峯巖峭險，既無崖谷，宛如全石。引正王為龍猛菩薩鑿此山中，建立伽藍。去山十數里，鑿開孔道，當其山下，仰鑿疏石。其中則長廊步簷，崇臺重閣，閣有五層，層有四院，竝建精舍，各鑄金像，量等佛身，妙窮工思，自餘莊嚴，唯飾金寶。從山高峯臨注飛泉，周流重閣，交帶廊廡。疎寮外穴，明燭中宇。初，引正王建此伽藍也，人力疲竭，府庫空虛，功猶未半，心甚憂慼。龍猛謂曰：「大王何故若有憂負？」王曰：「輒運大心，敢樹勝福，期之永固，待至慈氏。功績未成，財用已竭，每懷此恨，坐而待旦。」龍猛曰：「勿憂。崇福勝善，其利不窮，有興弘願，無憂不濟。今日還宮，當極歡樂，後晨出遊，歷覽山野，已而至此，平議營建。」王既受誨，奉以周旋。龍猛菩薩以神妙藥，滴諸大石，竝變為金。王遊見金，心口相賀，迴駕至龍猛所曰：「今日畋遊，神鬼所惑，山林之中，時見金聚。」龍猛曰：「非鬼惑也。至誠所感，故有此金，宜時取用，濟成勝業。」遂以營建，功畢有餘。於是五層之中，各鑄四大金像，餘尚盈積，充諸帑藏。招集千僧，居中禮誦。龍猛菩薩以釋迦佛所宣教法，及諸菩薩所演述論，鳩集部別，藏在其中。故上第一層唯置佛像及諸經論，下第五層居止淨人、資產、什物，中間三層僧徒所舍。聞諸先志曰：引正王營建已畢，計工人所食鹽價，用九拘胝（拘胝者，唐言億）金錢。其後僧徒忿諍，就王平議。時諸淨人更相謂曰：「僧徒諍起，言議相乖，凶人伺隙，毀壞伽藍。」於是重閣反拒，以擯僧徒。自爾已來，無復僧眾。遠矚山巖，莫知門徑。時引善醫方者入中療疾，蒙面入出，不識其路。
en_current: Three hundred or more li southwest of the country, one arrives at the mountain of Bhramaragiri (跋邏末羅耆釐山) (in Chinese, "Black Bee"). It rises abruptly and loftily, with precipitous peaks and cliffs; having neither slopes nor valleys, it appears to be a single solid rock. King Sātavāhana (引正王) excavated this mountain for the Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna (龍猛菩薩) to establish a monastery (saṃghārāma). Ten or more li from the mountain, a tunnel was excavated; directly beneath the mountain, they carved upward into the rock. Within it are long corridors and eaves, lofty terraces and multi-storied pavilions; the pavilions have five tiers, and each tier has four courtyards, all containing shrines (精舍) where golden images of the Buddha's size have been cast with exquisite craftsmanship, while the remaining decorations consist entirely of gold and jewels. From the high peaks of the mountain, a waterfall pours down, flowing around the multi-storied pavilions and winding through the corridors and verandas. Windows open through to the outside, letting light illuminate the interior. Initially, when King Sātavāhana was building this monastery, the labor force was exhausted and the treasury was empty; with the work not yet half finished, his heart was filled with deep sorrow. Nāgārjuna said to him, "Great King, why are you so burdened with worry?" The king replied, "I have given rise to a great aspiration and ventured to establish a supreme field of merit, hoping it would remain firm forever until the coming of Maitreya (慈氏). With the work not yet finished and the financial resources exhausted, I am constantly filled with this regret, sitting and waiting for the dawn." Nāgārjuna said, "Do not worry. The merit of cultivating such supreme goodness is inexhaustible; if one has raised a vast vow, there is no worry that it will not be fulfilled. Return to the palace today and enjoy yourself to the fullest; tomorrow morning, go out for an excursion, travel through the mountains and fields, and then come here to discuss the construction." The king, having received these instructions, followed them accordingly. The Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna (龍猛菩薩) used a miraculous medicine, dripping it onto large rocks, which all turned into gold. When the king saw the gold during his excursion, he rejoiced in his heart and words; he drove his carriage back to Nāgārjuna’s place and said, "During my outing today, I was deluded by spirits and ghosts, for I repeatedly saw heaps of gold amidst the mountains and forests." Nāgārjuna replied, "It was not a delusion of ghosts. It is the result of your utmost sincerity that this gold has appeared. You should take and use it immediately to complete your noble undertaking." He then proceeded with the construction, and when the work was finished, there was still a surplus. Thereupon, in each of the five tiers, he cast four large golden statues, and the remainder was still abundant, filling the treasuries. He summoned one thousand monks to reside within and perform rites and recitations. The Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna collected and classified the teachings proclaimed by Śākyamuni Buddha and the treatises composed by various Bodhisattvas, storing them within. Thus, the first tier at the top housed only Buddha images and various scriptures and treatises; the fifth tier at the bottom was for the residence of lay servants (淨人) and the storage of property and miscellaneous goods; and the three middle tiers were the lodgings for the monks. I have heard from the records of former sages that after King Sātavāhana had completed the construction, the cost of salt consumed by the workers was calculated to be nine koṭis (koṭi is, in Chinese, 億, a hundred million) of gold coins. Thereafter, the monks fell into disputes and went to the king to seek arbitration. At that time, the lay servants said to one another, "Since a quarrel has arisen among the monks and their arguments are contradictory, evil men will watch for an opening to destroy the monastery." Consequently, they barred the heavy doors to exclude the monks. From that time on, there has been no monastic community there. Looking at the mountain cliffs from afar, one cannot discern any gate or path. At times, those skilled in medical arts were brought inside to treat illnesses; they were blindfolded upon entering and exiting, and thus did not recognize the route.

zh: 從此大林中南行九百餘里，至案達羅國（南印度境）。案達羅國，周三千餘里。國大都城周二十餘里，號瓶耆羅。土地良沃，稼穡豐盛。氣序溫暑，風俗猛暴。語言辭調異中印度，至於文字，軌則大同。伽藍二十餘所，僧徒三千餘人。天祠三十餘所，異道寔多。瓶耆羅城側不遠有大伽藍，重閣層臺，製窮剞劂，佛像聖容，麗極工思。伽藍前有石窣堵波，高數百尺，並阿折羅（唐言所行）阿羅漢之所建也。所行羅漢伽藍西南不遠有窣堵波，無憂王之所建也，如來在昔於此說法，現大神通，度無量眾。
en_current: From here, traveling south through a great forest for more than nine hundred li, one arrives at the country of Āndhra (案達羅國) (within the borders of South India). The country of Āndhra is more than three thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is more than twenty li in circuit and is named Vengīpura (瓶耆羅). The land is fertile and rich, and the crops are abundant. The climate is warm and hot, and the customs of the people are fierce and impetuous. Their language and tone of speech differ from those of Central India, but as for their written characters, the rules are largely the same. There are more than twenty monasteries and over three thousand monks. There are more than thirty Deva temples, and the followers of heterodox paths are very numerous. Not far from the side of Vengīpura city is a large monastery with multi-storied pavilions and layered terraces, the craftsmanship of which exhausts the possibilities of carving; the sacred images of the Buddhas are of exquisite and ingenious design. In front of the monastery is a stone stūpa, several hundred feet high; both were built by the Arhat Ācāra (阿折羅) (in Chinese, "Conduct"). Not far to the southwest of the monastery of the Arhat Ācāra is a stūpa built by King Aśoka; in the past, the Tathāgata preached the Dharma here, manifested great supernatural powers, and delivered immeasurable multitudes.

zh: 所行羅漢伽藍西南行二十餘里，至孤山，山嶺有石窣堵波，陳那（唐言授）菩薩於此作《因明論》。陳那菩薩者，佛去世後，承風染衣。智願廣大，慧力深固，愍世無依，思弘聖教。以為因明之論，言深理廣，學者虛功，難以成業，乃匿迹幽巖，拪神寂定，觀述作之利害，審文義之繁約。是時崖谷震響，煙雲變釆，山神捧菩薩高數百尺，唱如是言：「昔佛世尊善權導物，以慈悲心，說《因明論》，綜括妙理，深究微言。如來寂滅，大義泯絕。今者，陳那菩薩福智悠遠，深達聖旨，因明之論，重弘茲日。」菩薩乃放大光明，照燭幽昧。時此國王深生尊敬，見此光明相，疑入金剛定，因請菩薩證無生果。陳那曰：「吾入定觀察，欲釋深經，心期正覺，非願無生果也。」王曰：「無生之果，眾聖欣仰，斷三界欲，洞三明智，斯盛事也，願疾證之。」陳那是時心悅王請，方欲證受無學聖果。時妙吉祥菩薩知而惜焉，欲相警誡，乃彈指悟之，而告曰：「惜哉！如何捨廣大心，為狹劣志，從獨善之懷，棄兼濟之願？欲為善利，當廣傳說慈氏菩薩所製《瑜伽師地論》，導誘後學，為利甚大。」陳那菩薩敬受指誨，奉以周旋。於是覃思沈研，廣因明論。猶恐學者懼其文微辭約也，乃舉其大義，綜其微言，作《因門論》，以導後進。自茲已後，宣暢瑜伽，盛業門人，有知當世。
en_current: Traveling more than twenty *li* southwest from the monastery of the Arhat Ācāra, one reaches a solitary hill. On the mountain ridge is a stone *stūpa* where the Bodhisattva Dignāga (陳那) (in Chinese, "Bestowed") composed the *Hetuvidyā-śāstra* (Treatise on Logic). As for the Bodhisattva Dignāga, after the Buddha had passed away, he followed the tradition and donned the dyed robes. His wisdom and vows were vast and great, and his power of discernment was deep and firm. Pitying the world for having no refuge, he contemplated how to propagate the sacred teachings. Considering that the treatises on logic were profound in language and extensive in reasoning, such that students labored in vain and found it difficult to achieve success, he hid his traces in secluded cliffs and settled his spirit in silent meditation, examining the merits and demerits of past works and scrutinizing the verbosity and conciseness of their meanings. At that time, the cliffs and valleys shook and echoed, the mist and clouds changed color, and a mountain god lifted the Bodhisattva up several hundred feet, proclaiming: "In the past, the Buddha, the World-Honored One, guided sentient beings through skillful means and, with a compassionate heart, preached the *Hetuvidyā-śāstra*, encompassing wonderful principles and investigating subtle words to their depths. Since the Tathāgata entered extinction, the great meaning has been cut off. Now, the Bodhisattva Dignāga, whose merit and wisdom are vast and far-reaching, and who deeply understands the sacred intent, shall once again propagate the *Hetuvidyā-śāstra* on this day." The Bodhisattva then emitted a great light, illuminating the darkness. At that time, the king of this country felt deep respect; seeing this manifestation of light, he suspected the Bodhisattva had entered the *vajra-samādhi* and therefore requested that the Bodhisattva certify the fruit of non-arising. Dignāga said: "I have entered meditation to observe and wish to explain the profound scriptures; my heart is set on perfect enlightenment, not on the fruit of non-arising." The king said: "The fruit of non-arising is something all sages admire; it severs the desires of the three realms and provides mastery of the three types of supernormal knowledge—this is a magnificent achievement, and I hope you will realize it quickly." At that time, Dignāga (陳那) was pleased by the king’s request and was about to realize and accept the holy fruit of the *aśaikṣa* (no-more-learning). At that moment, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī (妙吉祥菩薩) knew of this and felt it was a pity; wishing to warn him, he snapped his fingers to awaken him and said: "What a pity! How can you abandon the vast and great mind for a narrow and inferior intention, following a desire for individual salvation while discarding the vow to benefit others? If you wish to perform a virtuous benefit, you should widely propagate the *Yogācārabhūmi-śāstra* (瑜伽師地論) composed by the Bodhisattva Maitreya (慈氏菩薩) to guide and encourage later students; the benefit of this is truly great." The Bodhisattva Dignāga respectfully accepted this instruction and followed it faithfully. Thereupon, he pondered deeply and researched extensively the treatises on *hetuvidyā* (logic). Fearing that students might be intimidated by the subtlety of the text and the conciseness of the language, he extracted the essential meanings and synthesized the profound words to compose the *Nyāyamukha* (因門論) in order to guide those who would come after. From this time forward, he propagated the *Yogācāra* (瑜伽), and his flourishing work and disciples were known throughout the world.

name_zh: 阿折羅阿羅漢伽藍・石窣堵波
zh: 瓶耆羅城側不遠有大伽藍，重閣層臺，製窮剞劂，佛像聖容，麗極工思。伽藍前有石窣堵波，高數百尺，並阿折羅（唐言所行）阿羅漢之所建也。
en_current: Not far from the side of the city of Veṅgī (瓶耆羅城) there is a great monastery, with storeyed pavilions and tiered terraces, carved with the utmost skill; the images and holy forms of the Buddha are of surpassing beauty and craftsmanship. In front of the monastery there is a stone stūpa several hundred feet high; both were built by the arhat Ācāra (阿折羅) (in Chinese, 'he who practises', 所行).

zh: 從此林野中南行千餘里，至馱那羯磔迦國（亦謂大安達邏國。南印度境）。馱那羯磔迦國，周六千餘里。國大都城周四十餘里。土地膏腴，稼穡殷盛。荒野多，邑居少。氣序溫暑，人貌釐黑。性猛烈，好學藝。伽藍鱗次，荒蕪已甚，存者二十餘所，僧徒千餘人，並多習學大眾部法。天祠百餘所，異道寔多。
en_current: From this forest and wilderness, traveling south for more than a thousand *li*, one arrives at the country of Dhānakaṭaka (馱那羯磔迦國; also called the Great Andhra country; it is within the borders of South India). The country of Dhānakaṭaka is more than six thousand *li* in circuit. The capital city of the country is more than forty *li* in circuit. The land is fertile and rich, and the crops are abundant. There is much wilderness and few settlements. The climate is warm and hot, and the people are dark in complexion. Their nature is fierce and impetuous, and they are fond of learning the arts. The monasteries are arranged like the scales of a fish, but they are already very desolate; those that remain number more than twenty, with over a thousand monks, all of whom mostly study the teachings of the Mahāsāṃghika school. There are more than a hundred Deva temples, and the followers of heterodox paths are very numerous.

zh: 城東據山有弗婆勢羅（唐言東山）僧伽藍，城西據山有阿伐羅勢羅（唐言西山）僧伽藍，此國先王為佛建焉。奠川通徑，疏崖峙閣，長廊步簷，枕巖接岫，靈神警衛，聖賢遊息。自佛寂滅，千年之內，每歲有千凡夫僧同入安居，其解安居日，皆證羅漢，以神通力凌虛而去；千年之後，凡、聖同居；自百餘年，無復僧侶，而山神易形，或作豺狼，或為猨狖，驚恐行人，以故空荒，閴無僧眾。
en_current: To the east of the city, resting on a mountain, is the Pūrvaśaila (弗婆勢羅) (in Chinese, "Eastern Mountain") Monastery; to the west of the city, resting on a mountain, is the Avaraśaila (阿伐羅勢羅) (in Chinese, "Western Mountain") Monastery. These were built for the Buddha by a former king of this country. The streams were regulated and paths opened, with pavilions perched upon cleared cliffs, and long corridors and covered walkways resting against the rocks and joining the peaks; they are guarded by divine spirits and frequented by sages and saints. Within the millennium following the Buddha’s nirvana, a thousand ordinary monks would gather each year to enter the summer retreat; on the day the retreat concluded, they would all attain arhatship and depart by rising into the air through their supernatural powers. After the millennium, ordinary and holy monks lived there together. For over a hundred years, there have been no more monks, and the mountain spirits have changed their forms—sometimes appearing as jackals and wolves, other times as apes and monkeys—to terrify travelers; for this reason, the place is desolate and devoid of any monastic community.

zh: 城西據山有阿伐羅勢羅（唐言西山）僧伽藍，此國先王為佛建焉。奠川通徑，疏崖峙閣，長廊步簷，枕巖接岫，靈神警衛，聖賢遊息。自佛寂滅，千年之內，每歲有千凡夫僧同入安居，其解安居日，皆證羅漢，以神通力凌虛而去；千年之後，凡、聖同居；自百餘年，無復僧侶，而山神易形，或作豺狼，或為猨狖，驚恐行人，以故空荒，閴無僧眾。
en_current: To the west of the city, resting on a mountain, is the Avaraśaila (阿伐羅勢羅) (in Chinese, "West Mountain") Monastery, which a former king of this country built for the Buddha. The stream was regulated and paths opened, with cliffs cleared to support pavilions, long corridors, and covered walkways, all resting against the crags and joining the peaks; divine spirits guard and protect it, and sages and saints have frequented it to rest. Within the millennium following the Buddha’s nirvana, a thousand ordinary monks would enter the summer retreat there together each year; on the day the retreat concluded, they would all attain arhatship and depart by rising into the void through their supernatural powers. After that millennium, ordinary monks and holy ones lived there together. For the past hundred years or so, there have been no more monks, and the mountain spirits have changed their forms—sometimes appearing as jackals or wolves, other times as apes or monkeys—to terrify travelers. For this reason, the place has become desolate and is devoid of any monastic community.

zh: 城南不遠有大山巖，婆毘吠伽（唐言清辯）論師住阿素洛宮待見慈氏菩薩成佛之處。論師雅量弘遠，至德深邃，外示僧佉之服，內弘龍猛之學。聞摩揭陀國護法菩薩宣揚法教，學徒數千，有懷談議，杖錫而往。至波吒釐城，知護法菩薩在菩提樹，論師乃命門人曰：「汝行詣菩提樹護法菩薩所，如我辭曰：『菩薩宣揚遺教，導誘迷徒，仰德虛心，為日已久。然以宿願未果，遂乖禮謁。菩提樹者，誓不空見，見當有證，稱天人師。』」護法菩薩謂其使曰：「人世如幻，身命若浮，渴日勤誠，未遑談議。」人信往復，竟不會見。論師既還本土，靜而思曰：「非慈氏成佛，誰決我疑？」於觀自在菩薩像前誦《隨心陀羅尼》，絕粒飲水，時歷三歲。觀自在菩薩乃現妙色身，謂論師曰：「何所志乎？」對曰：「願留此身，待見慈氏。」觀自在菩薩曰：「人命危脆，世間浮幻，宜修勝善願，生覩史多天，於斯禮覲，尚速待見。」論師曰：「志不可奪，心不可貳。」菩薩曰：「若然者，宜往馱那羯磔迦國城南山巖執金剛神所，至誠誦持《執金剛陀羅尼》者，當遂此願。」論師於是往而誦焉。三歲之後，神乃謂曰：「伊何所願，若此勤勵？」論師曰：「願留此身，待見慈氏。觀自在菩薩指遣來請，成我願者，其在神乎？」神乃授祕方，而謂之曰：「此巖石內有阿素洛宮，如法行請，石壁當開，開即入中，可以待見。」論師曰：「幽居無覩，詎知佛興？」執金剛曰：「慈氏出世，我當相報。」論師受命，專精誦持，復歷三歲，初無異想，呪芥子以擊石，巖壁豁而洞開。是時百千萬眾觀覩忘返，論師跨其戶而告眾曰：「吾久祈請，待見慈氏，聖靈警祐，大願斯遂，宜可入此，同見佛興。」聞者怖駭，莫敢履戶，謂是毒蛇之窟，恐喪身命。再三告語，唯有六人從入。論師顧謝時眾，從容而入，入之既已，石壁還合，眾皆怨嗟，恨前言之過也。
en_current: Not far to the south of the city is a great mountain crag, the place where the master of treatises Bhāviveka (婆毘吠伽) (in Chinese, Qingbian, "Clear Discrimination") resided in the palace of the Asuras, awaiting the appearance of Maitreya Bodhisattva to attain Buddhahood. The master of treatises possessed a refined character that was vast and far-reaching, and his supreme virtue was profound and deep; outwardly he displayed the attire of the Sāṃkhya, while inwardly he promoted the teachings of Nāgārjuna. Hearing that the Bodhisattva Dharmapāla in the country of Magadha was propagating the teachings of the Dharma and had several thousand students, he felt a desire to engage in discussion, so he took up his staff and set out. Upon arriving at the city of Pāṭaliputra, he learned that the Bodhisattva Dharmapāla was at the Bodhi Tree. The master of treatises then instructed his disciple, saying: "Go to the place of the Bodhisattva Dharmapāla at the Bodhi Tree and convey my words as follows: 'The Bodhisattva propagates the bequeathed teachings and guides the deluded; I have long looked up to your virtue with a humble mind. However, because my past vows have not yet been fulfilled, I have missed the opportunity to pay my respects. As for the Bodhi Tree, I vow not to see it in vain; when I see it, I shall attain realization and be called the Teacher of gods and men.'" The Bodhisattva Dharmapāla said to his messenger: "The human world is like an illusion, and life is like a floating bubble; all day long I strive earnestly and have no time for discussion." Messengers went back and forth, but they never met. After the master of treatises returned to his native land, he reflected in silence: "If Maitreya does not attain Buddhahood, who can resolve my doubts?" Before an image of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, he recited the *Hṛdaya-dhāraṇī* (隨心陀羅尼), abstaining from grain and drinking only water for a period of three years. Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva then manifested a wondrous physical form and said to the master of treatises: "What is your aspiration?" He replied, "I wish to preserve this body to wait until I see Maitreya (慈氏)." Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva said, "Human life is precarious and fragile, and the world is a floating illusion; you should cultivate superior and virtuous vows to be reborn in the Tuṣita Heaven (覩史多天), where you may pay homage and meet him more quickly." The master of treatises said, "My will cannot be swayed, and my heart cannot be divided." The Bodhisattva said, "If that is the case, you should go to the mountain cave south of the city of the country of Dhānyakaṭaka (馱那羯磔迦國) to the abode of the Vajrapāṇi (執金剛) deity; if you recite the *Vajrapāṇi-dhāraṇī* (執金剛陀羅尼) with utmost sincerity, this vow shall be fulfilled." The master of treatises then went there and recited it. After three years, the deity asked him, "What is your wish, that you are so diligent and earnest?" The master of treatises said, "I wish to preserve this body to wait until I see Maitreya. Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva directed me to come and request your aid; is it not in your power to fulfill my vow?" The deity then bestowed a secret method upon him and said, "Inside this rock is the Asura Palace (阿素洛宮); if you perform the ritual according to the Dharma and make your request, the stone wall shall open. Once it opens, you may enter and wait there to see him." The master of treatises said, "If I dwell in seclusion and see nothing, how will I know when the Buddha has arisen?" The Vajrapāṇi deity replied, "When Maitreya appears in the world, I shall inform you." The master of treatises accepted this instruction and practiced the recitation with focused intensity. After another three years had passed, without ever having a different thought, he enchanted mustard seeds and struck the rock with them; the stone wall suddenly split open. At that time, hundreds of thousands of people watched, forgetting to return home.
