It is suitable for cattle, sheep, camels, mules, and similar livestock. The people are impetuous and do not like to study. Their language differs slightly from that of Mid-India. Their customs are simple and honest, and they revere the Three Jewels. There are more than eighty saṃghārāmas and over five thousand monks, most of whom study the teachings of the Sāṃmitīya school of the Lesser Vehicle. There are ten deva temples, mostly inhabited by ash-smearing heterodox ascetics. In the city, there is a temple to Maheśvara (大自在天). The temple is carved and adorned, and the image of the deity is spiritually responsive; ash-smearing heterodox ascetics reside within it. In the past, the Tathāgata traveled extensively in this country, preaching the Dharma to save people and guiding the commoners to benefit the populace; therefore, King Aśoka (無憂王) built six stūpas at the sites of these sacred traces.

zh: 從此西行，減二千里，至狼揭羅國（西印度境）。狼揭羅國，東西南北各數千里。國大都城周三十餘里，號窣菟黎濕伐羅。土地沃潤，稼穡滋盛。氣序風俗，同阿點婆翅羅國。居人殷盛，多諸珍寶。臨大海濱，入西女國之路也。無大君長，據川自立，不相承命，役屬波剌斯國。文字大同印度，語言少異。邪正兼信。伽藍百餘所，僧徒六千餘人，大小二乘，兼功習學。天祠數百所，塗灰外道，其徒極眾。城中有大自在天祠，莊嚴壯麗，塗灰外道之所宗事。
en_current: Traveling west from here for less than two thousand li, one reaches the country of Laṅgala (狼揭羅國) (within the borders of Western India). The country of Laṅgala measures several thousand li in each of the four directions. The capital city is over thirty li in circumference and is named Sthūlīśvara (窣菟黎濕伐羅). The land is fertile and moist, and crops are abundant. The climate and customs are the same as those of the country of Audumbatira (阿點婆翅羅國). The inhabitants are prosperous and possess many precious treasures. It borders the great ocean and is the route to the country of the Western Women (西女國). There is no great monarch; the people occupy the river valleys and establish themselves independently, not acknowledging the authority of one another, and are subject to the country of Pārsi (波剌斯國). Their writing is largely the same as that of India, though their spoken language differs slightly. They believe in both heterodox and orthodox teachings. There are over one hundred monasteries with more than six thousand monks, who study and practice the teachings of both the Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna. There are several hundred Deva temples, and the ash-smearing heretics are extremely numerous. Inside the city is a temple of Maheśvara (大自在天), magnificent and grand, which is the place of worship for the ash-smearing heretics.

zh: 自此西北，至波剌斯國（雖非印度之國，路次附見。舊曰波斯，略也）。波剌斯國，周數萬里。國大都城號蘇剌薩儻那，周四十餘里。川土既多，氣序亦異，大抵溫也。引水為田，人戶富饒。出金、鍮石、頗胝、水精、奇珍異寶，工織大錦、細褐、氍毺之類，多善馬、槖駝。貨用大銀錢。人性躁暴，俗無禮義。文字、語言異於諸國。無學藝，多工技，凡諸造作，隣境所重。婚姻雜亂，死多棄屍。其形偉大，齊髮露頭，衣皮褐，服錦㲲。戶課賦稅，人四銀錢。天祠甚多，提那跋外道之徒為所宗也。伽藍二三，僧徒數百，並學小乘教說一切有部法。釋迦佛鉢在此王宮。
en_current: From here, going northwest, one reaches the country of Pārsa (波剌斯國) (although it is not a country of India, it is appended here as it lies along the route; the old name was Bosi (波斯), which is an abbreviation). The country of Pārsa is several tens of thousands of li in circumference. The great capital city of the country is named Sūlāsātǎngnà (蘇剌薩儻那), which is more than forty li in circumference. The land is vast and the climate is also distinct, being generally warm. Water is diverted to irrigate the fields, and the households are wealthy and prosperous. It produces gold, brass, quartz, crystal, and rare treasures and precious gems. The people are skilled at weaving large brocades, fine woolens, and rugs, and there are many fine horses and camels. For currency, they use large silver coins. The nature of the people is impetuous and violent, and their customs lack propriety and righteousness. Their script and language differ from those of other countries. They have no interest in academic arts but are skilled in crafts; all their manufactures are highly valued by neighboring regions. Marriages are promiscuous, and when people die, they are mostly abandoned as corpses. The people are large in stature, wear their hair cut level, and go bareheaded; they wear leather and wool garments and dress in brocade and felt. Regarding household taxes and levies, each person pays four silver coins. There are many deva temples, and the followers of the Dinaba (提那跋) heretics are those who revere them. There are two or three saṃghārāmas with several hundred monks, all of whom study the Hīnayāna teachings of the Sarvāstivāda school. The alms bowl of the Śākya Buddha is in the king’s palace here.

zh: 國東境有鶴秣城，內城不廣，外郭周六十餘里。居人眾，家產富。
en_current: On the eastern border of the country is the city of Hūma (鶴秣城); the inner city is not extensive, but the outer wall is more than sixty li in circuit. The inhabitants are numerous, and their households are wealthy.

zh: 西北接拂懍國，境壤風俗，同波剌斯。形貌語言，稍有乖異，多珍寶，亦富饒也。
en_current: To the northwest it borders the country of Hrom (拂懍國); its territory and customs are the same as those of Persia (波剌斯). Its physical appearance and language are slightly different; it possesses many rare treasures and is also very wealthy.

zh: 拂懍國西南海島有西女國，皆是女人，略無男子。多諸珍貨，附拂懍國，故拂懍王歲遣丈夫配焉，其俗產男皆不舉也。
en_current: On an island in the sea to the southwest of the country of Fulin (拂懍國), there is the Western Women’s Country. It is inhabited entirely by women, and there are virtually no men. It possesses many precious goods and is a dependency of the country of Fulin; therefore, the King of Fulin sends men there every year to mate with them, and it is their custom not to raise any male children who are born.

zh: 自阿點婆翅羅國北行七百餘里，至臂多縶羅國（西印度境）。臂多縶羅國，周三千餘里。國大都城周二十餘里。居人殷盛，無大君長，役屬信度國。土地沙鹵，寒風淒勁。多宿、麥，少花菓。而風俗獷暴。語異中印度。不好藝學，然知淳信。伽藍五十餘所，僧徒三千餘人，並學小乘正量部法。天祠二十餘所，並塗灰外道也。城北十五六里大林中，有窣堵波，高數百尺，無憂王所建也。中有舍利，時放光明。是如來昔作仙人，為國王所害之處。此東不遠有故伽藍，是昔大迦多延那大阿羅漢之所建立。其傍則有過去四佛座及經行遺迹之處，建窣堵波以為旌表。
en_current: Traveling north from the country of Audumbatira (阿點婆翅羅國) for more than seven hundred *li*, one arrives at the country of Pi-to-zhi-luo (臂多縶羅國) (within the borders of Western India). The country of Pi-to-zhi-luo is more than three thousand *li* in circuit. The capital city is more than twenty *li* in circuit. The inhabitants are numerous and prosperous; they have no great sovereign but are subject to the country of Sindhu (信度國). The land is sandy and saline, and the cold winds are biting. There is much winter wheat, but few flowers or fruits. The customs of the people are fierce and violent. Their language differs from that of Central India. They do not care for the arts or learning, yet they are sincere in their faith. There are more than fifty monasteries with over three thousand monks, all of whom study the teachings of the Sāmmitīya school of the Lesser Vehicle. There are more than twenty *deva* temples, all belonging to the ash-smearing non-Buddhists. In a large forest fifteen or sixteen *li* north of the city, there is a *stūpa* several hundred feet high, built by King Aśoka. Inside it are relics that occasionally emit light. This is the place where the Tathāgata, in a former life as a *ṛṣi*, was harmed by a king. Not far to the east of this is an old monastery, which was established by the great arhat Mahākātyāyana. Beside it are the seats and walking paths of the four past Buddhas, where *stūpas* have been built to mark the sites.

zh: 從此東北行三百餘里，至阿軬荼國（西印度境）。阿軬荼國，周二千四五百里。國大都城周二十餘里。無大君長，役屬信度國。土宜稼穡，宿、麥特豐，花菓少，草木疎。氣序風寒，人性獷烈。言辭朴質，不尚學業，然於三寶守心淳信。伽藍二十餘所，僧徒二千餘人，多學小乘正量部法。天祠五所，並塗灰外道也。城東北不遠，大竹林中，伽藍餘趾，是如來昔於此處聽諸苾芻著亟縛屣（唐言靴）。傍有窣堵波，無憂王所建也，基雖傾陷，尚高百餘尺。其傍精舍，有青石立佛像，每至齋日，或放神光。次南八百餘步，林中有窣堵波，無憂王之所建也。如來昔日止此，夜寒，乃以三衣重覆，至明旦，開諸苾芻著複納衣。此林之中有佛經行之處。又有諸窣堵波，鱗次相望，並過去四佛坐處也。其窣堵波中有如來髮、爪，每至齋日，多放光明。
en_current: From here, traveling northeast for more than three hundred li, one arrives at the country of Avaṇḍa (阿軬荼國) (in the region of West India). The country of Avaṇḍa is two thousand four or five hundred li in circuit. The capital city is over twenty li in circuit. There is no great monarch; it is subject to the country of Sindhu (信度國). The land is suitable for agriculture; winter wheat is especially abundant, while flowers and fruits are scarce, and trees and vegetation are sparse. The climate is windy and cold, and the nature of the people is fierce and impetuous. Their speech is simple and plain, and they do not value academic pursuits, yet they are pure and faithful in their devotion to the Three Jewels. There are over twenty saṃghārāmas with more than two thousand monks, most of whom study the teachings of the Hīnayāna Saṃmitīya school. There are five Deva temples, all belonging to the ash-smearing heretics. Not far to the northeast of the city, in a large bamboo grove, are the remaining foundations of a saṃghārāma; this is where the Tathāgata once permitted the bhikṣus to wear *jīvashī* (亟縛屣) (in Tang language: boots). Beside it is a stūpa built by King Aśoka; although the base has collapsed, it is still over one hundred feet high. In the *vihāra* (精舍) beside it, there is a standing Buddha image made of blue stone, which sometimes emits divine light on fast days. Eight hundred paces further south, in the forest, there is a stūpa built by King Aśoka. The Tathāgata once stayed here; because the night was cold, he covered himself with his three robes, and the next morning, he permitted the bhikṣus to wear quilted robes. In this forest, there is a place where the Buddha walked in meditation. There are also several stūpas, arranged like fish scales facing one another, which are the places where the four past Buddhas sat. Inside that stūpa are the hair and nail relics of the Tathāgata, which often emit divine light on fast days.

zh: 從此東北行九百餘里，至伐剌拏國（西印度境）。伐剌拏國，周四千餘里。國大都城周二十餘里。居人殷盛，役屬迦畢試國。地多山林，稼穡時播。氣序微寒，風俗獷烈。性急暴，志鄙弊。語言少同中印度。邪正兼崇，不好學藝。伽藍數十，荒圮已多，僧徒三百餘人，並學大乘法教。天祠五所，多塗灰外道也。城南不遠有故伽藍，如來在昔於此說法，示教利喜，開悟含生。其側有過去四佛座及經行遺迹之處。聞諸土俗曰：從此國西接稽畺那國，居大山間川，別立主，無大君長。多羊、馬，有善馬者，其形姝大，諸國希種，隣境所寶。復此西北，踰大山，涉廣川，歷小城邑，行二千餘里，出印度境，至漕矩吒國（亦謂漕利國）。
en_current: From here, traveling northeast for more than nine hundred li, one reaches the country of Varaṇa (伐剌拏國) (in the territory of West India). The country of Varaṇa is over four thousand li in circuit. The capital city is more than twenty li in circuit. The inhabitants are numerous and prosperous, and they are subject to the country of Kāpiśī (迦畢試國). The land has many mountains and forests, and crops are sown in their proper seasons. The climate is slightly cold, and the customs are fierce and violent. The people are impetuous and irritable, and their dispositions are base and corrupt. Their language is somewhat similar to that of Mid-India. They revere both heterodox and orthodox teachings, and they do not care for learning or the arts. There are several dozen monasteries, most of which are ruined and desolate; there are over three hundred monks, all of whom study the teachings of the Mahāyāna. There are five Deva temples, mostly belonging to the ash-smearing ascetics. Not far to the south of the city is an old monastery where the Tathāgata in the past preached the Dharma, manifesting teachings to bring benefit and joy, and enlightening living beings. Beside it are the seats of the four past Buddhas and the places where they walked in meditation. I have heard from the local people that to the west of this country, bordering the country of Jīmna (稽畺那國), the people live in the valleys among the great mountains; they have separate rulers and no great monarch. There are many sheep and horses. Those who possess good horses have animals that are large and beautiful in form; they are a rare breed among the various countries and are treasured by the neighboring regions. Traveling northwest from here again, crossing great mountains, traversing wide rivers, and passing through small towns and cities, one travels over two thousand li, leaves the borders of India, and reaches the country of Jāguḍa (漕矩吒國) (also called the country of Caoli (漕利國)).

zh: 聞諸土俗曰：從此國西接稽畺那國，居大山間川，別立主，無大君長。多羊、馬，有善馬者，其形姝大，諸國希種，隣境所寶。
en_current: According to local accounts, to the west of this country one reaches the country of Kaikanan (稽畺那國); it is situated among the valleys of the great mountains, and it has separate local chieftains but no sovereign ruler. It abounds in sheep and horses, and among the horses are those of excellent quality, whose forms are remarkably large; they are a rare breed among the nations and are prized by neighboring regions.

zh: 漕矩吒國，周七千餘里。國大都城號鶴悉那，周三十餘里，或都鶴薩羅城，城周三十餘里，並堅峻險固也。山川隱軫，疇壟爽塏。穀稼時播，宿麥滋豐，草木扶疎，花菓茂盛，宜欝金香，出興瞿草，草生羅摩印度川。鶴薩羅城中踊泉流派，國人利之，以溉田也。氣序寒烈，霜雪繁多。人性輕躁，情多詭詐。好學藝，多技術，聽而不明，日誦數萬言。文字言辭，異於諸國。多飾虛談，少成事實。雖祀百神，敬崇三寶。伽藍數百所，僧徒萬餘人，並皆習學大乘法教。今王淳信，累葉承統，務興勝福，敏而好學。無憂王所建窣堵波十餘所。天祠數十，異道雜居。計多外道，其徒極盛，宗事䅳（錫苟反，下同）那天。其天神昔自迦畢試國阿路猱山徙居此國南界䅳那呬羅山中，作威作福，為暴為惡，信求者遂願，輕蔑者招殃。故遠近宗仰，上下祗懼。隣國異俗君臣僚庶，每歲嘉辰不期而會，或齎金、銀、奇寶，或以牛、馬、馴畜，競興貢奉，俱伸誠素。所以金、銀布地，羊馬滿谷，無敢覬覦，唯修施奉。宗事外道，克心苦行，天神授其呪術，外道遵行多効，治療疾病，頗蒙痊愈。
en_current: The country of Jaguḍa (漕矩吒國) is over seven thousand li in circuit. The great capital city of the country is called Ghasna (鶴悉那), which is over thirty li in circuit; sometimes the capital is at the city of Ghasala (鶴薩羅城), which is also over thirty li in circuit, and both are steep, rugged, and well-fortified. The mountains and rivers are undulating, and the fields and ridges are high and dry. Crops are sown in their proper seasons, winter wheat grows in abundance, vegetation is lush, and flowers and fruits are flourishing. The land is suitable for saffron (欝金香), and it produces the hingu herb (興瞿草), which grows in the Rāmēndu (羅摩印度) valley. In the city of Ghasala, there are gushing springs that flow in various directions, which the people of the country utilize to irrigate their fields. The climate is cold and harsh, with frequent frost and snow. The people are impulsive by nature and their dispositions are often deceitful. They are fond of learning arts and possess many technical skills; they listen but do not understand, yet they can recite tens of thousands of words a day. Their script and language differ from those of other countries. They often embellish empty talk and accomplish few practical results. Although they worship the hundred gods, they revere and honor the Three Jewels. There are several hundred monasteries and more than ten thousand monks, all of whom study the teachings of the Mahāyāna. The present king is sincere in his faith, having inherited the throne through successive generations; he is devoted to performing meritorious deeds, and is intelligent and fond of learning. There are more than ten stūpas built by King Aśoka (無憂王). There are several dozen deva temples, where followers of different sects live together. Most of the people are non-Buddhists, and their disciples are extremely numerous; they worship the deity Śuna (䅳那) (䅳 is pronounced by the *fanqie* 錫苟, i.e. the initial of 錫 with the final of 苟; likewise below). This deity formerly moved from Mount Aruṇa (阿路猱山) in the country of Kāpiśī (迦畢試國) to reside in Mount Śunāśīra (䅳那呬羅山) on the southern border of this country, where he displays his power, bestows blessings, and commits acts of violence and evil; those who believe and pray to him have their wishes fulfilled, while those who despise him incur calamity. Thus, those far and near revere him, and those high and low stand in awe of him. The rulers, ministers, officials, and commoners of neighboring countries with different customs gather without appointment on auspicious days each year; they bring gold, silver, and rare treasures, or offer cattle, horses, and domestic animals, competing to present offerings to express their sincerity. Consequently, gold and silver are spread upon the ground and sheep and horses fill the valleys, yet no one dares to covet them, as all are intent only on making offerings. Those who follow non-Buddhist paths and practice asceticism with a disciplined heart are granted incantations by the celestial deity; the non-Buddhists who practice them find them highly effective, and those treated for illnesses are often healed.

zh: 國大都城號鶴悉那，周三十餘里，或都鶴薩羅城，城周三十餘里，並堅峻險固也。
en_current: The great capital city of the country is called Ghasna (鶴悉那), which is over thirty li in circuit; sometimes the capital is at the city of Ghasala (鶴薩羅), which is also over thirty li in circuit, and both are steep, rugged, and well-fortified.

zh: 或都鶴薩羅城，城周三十餘里，並堅峻險固也。山川隱軫，疇壟爽塏。穀稼時播，宿麥滋豐，草木扶疎，花菓茂盛，宜欝金香，出興瞿草，草生羅摩印度川。鶴薩羅城中踊泉流派，國人利之，以溉田也。
en_current: Or the capital is the city of Ghasala (鶴薩羅城), the city circuit is over thirty *li*, and it is both steep, rugged, and well-fortified. The mountains and rivers are undulating, and the fields and ridges are high and dry. Grain crops are sown in their proper seasons, winter wheat grows in abundance, vegetation is lush, and flowers and fruits are flourishing. It is suitable for saffron (*kuṅkuma*), and produces the *hingu* herb; this herb grows in the Rāmēndu (羅摩印度) river valley. In the city of Ghasala, gushing springs flow in various directions, and the people of the country benefit from them to irrigate their fields.

zh: 穀稼時播，宿麥滋豐，草木扶疎，花菓茂盛，宜欝金香，出興瞿草，草生羅摩印度川。
en_current: Crops are sown in their proper seasons, winter wheat grows in abundance, vegetation is lush, and flowers and fruits are flourishing. The land is suitable for saffron (kuṅkuma) and produces the hingu herb; this herb grows in the Rāmēndu (羅摩印度川) valley.

zh: 從此北行五百餘里，至弗栗恃薩儻那國。弗栗恃薩儻那國，東西二千餘里，南北千餘里。國大都城號護苾那，周二十餘里。土宜風俗，同漕矩吒國，語言有異。氣序寒勁，人性獷烈。王，突厥種也，深信三寶，尚學遵德。
en_current: From here, traveling northward for more than five hundred li, one arrives at the country of Vṛjiṣṭhāna (弗栗恃薩儻那國). The country of Vṛjiṣṭhāna is more than two thousand li from east to west and over one thousand li from north to south. The capital city of the country is named Hūbīnā (護苾那), and it is more than twenty li in circuit. The soil, products, and customs are the same as those of the country of Jaguḍa (漕矩吒國), though the language is different. The climate is cold and harsh, and the temperament of the people is fierce and impetuous. The king is of Turkic lineage; he has deep faith in the Three Jewels, values learning, and adheres to virtue.

zh: 國大都城號護苾那，周二十餘里。
en_current: The capital city of the country is called Hubina (護苾那), and it is over twenty li in circuit.

zh: 從此國東北，踰山涉川，越迦畢試國邊城小邑，凡數十所，至大雪山婆羅犀那大嶺。嶺極崇峻，危隥𢼨傾，蹊徑盤迂，巖岫回互。或入深谷，或上高崖，盛夏合凍，鑿氷而度。行經三日，方至嶺上。寒風凄烈，積雪彌谷，行旅經涉，莫能佇足。飛隼翱翔，不能越度，足趾步履，然後飜飛，下望諸山，若觀培塿。贍部洲中，斯嶺特高。其巔無樹，唯多石峯，攢立叢倚，森然若林。
en_current: Proceeding northeast from this country, crossing mountains and fording rivers, and passing through several dozen small frontier towns of the country of Kāpiśī (迦畢試國), one reaches the Varasena (婆羅犀那) great range of the Great Snow Mountains. The range is extremely high and steep, with dangerous, precipitous slopes; the paths are winding and the cliffs and peaks interlock. Sometimes one enters deep valleys, and sometimes one ascends high precipices; even in the height of summer it is frozen over, and one must hack through the ice to cross. After traveling for three days, one finally reaches the top of the range. The cold wind is bitter and fierce, and accumulated snow fills the valleys; travelers passing through cannot find a place to stand. Soaring falcons cannot fly across it; they must walk on their feet before taking flight again. Looking down at the various mountains, they appear like small anthills. In the Jambudvīpa (贍部洲), this range is exceptionally high. Its summit has no trees, but only many stone peaks, clustered and leaning against one another, standing dense like a forest.

zh: 又三日行，方得下嶺，至安呾羅縛國。安呾羅縛國，覩貨邏國故地。周三千餘里。國大都城周十四五里。無大君長，役屬突厥。山阜連屬，川田隘狹。氣序寒烈，風雪凄勁。豐稼穡，宜花菓。人性獷暴，俗無綱紀。不知罪福，不尚習學，唯修神祠，少信佛法。伽藍三所，僧徒數十，然皆遵習大眾部法。有一窣堵波，無憂王建也。
en_current: After traveling for three more days, I finally descended from the mountain range and reached the country of Antarava (安呾羅縛國). The country of Antarava is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is over three thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is fourteen or fifteen li in circuit. There is no great sovereign or leader, and it is subject to the Turks. The mountains and hills are connected, and the river valleys and fields are narrow and confined. The climate is cold and severe, and the wind and snow are biting and harsh. It is abundant in crops and suitable for flowers and fruits. The nature of the people is fierce and violent, and their customs lack order and discipline. They do not understand the concepts of sin or merit, and they do not value learning; they only maintain shrines to deities and have little faith in the Buddha-dharma. There are three monasteries with several dozen monks, all of whom follow the teachings of the Mahāsāṃghika school. There is one stūpa, which was built by King Aśoka.

zh: 從此西北，入谷踰嶺，度諸小城，行四百餘里，至闊悉多國。闊悉多國，覩貨邏國故地也。周減千里。國大都城周十餘里。無大君長，役屬突厥。山多川狹，風而且寒。穀稼豐，花菓盛。人性獷暴，俗無法度。伽藍三所，僧徒尠少。
en_current: From here, traveling northwest, entering valleys and crossing ridges, and passing through various small towns for over four hundred li, one reaches the country of Khost (闊悉多國). The country of Khost is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is less than one thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is over ten li in circuit. There is no great monarch, and it is subject to the Turks (突厥). The mountains are numerous and the rivers narrow; it is windy and cold. The grain crops are abundant, and flowers and fruits are plentiful. The nature of the people is fierce and violent, and their customs lack laws and regulations. There are three saṃghārāmas (伽藍), and the number of monks is very small.

zh: 從此西北，踰山越谷，度諸城邑，行三百餘里，至活國。活國，覩貨邏國故地也。周二千餘里。國大都城周二十餘里。無別君長，役屬突厥。上地平坦，穀稼時播，草木榮茂，花菓具繁。氣序和暢，風俗淳質。人性躁烈，衣服氈褐。多信三寶，少事諸神。伽藍十餘所，僧徒數百人，大小二乘，兼功綜習。其王，突厥也，管鐵門已南諸小國，遷徙鳥居，不常其邑。
en_current: From here, going northwest across mountains and valleys and passing through various towns for over three hundred li, one arrives at the country of Huoh (活國). The country of Huoh is the ancient territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is over two thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is over twenty li in circuit. It has no separate ruler, being subject to the Turks (突厥). The land is level and flat; grain is sown in its season, vegetation is lush and flourishing, and flowers and fruits are abundant. The climate is mild and pleasant, and the customs are simple and honest. The people are impetuous and fierce by nature, and they wear garments of felt and coarse wool. They mostly believe in the Three Jewels and rarely worship other gods. There are more than ten monasteries and several hundred monks, who study both the Mahāyāna and Hīnayāna teachings. Their king is a Turk who governs the various small countries south of the Iron Gate (鐵門); he moves about like a bird and has no permanent seat of government.

zh: 從此東入葱嶺。葱嶺者，據贍部洲中，南接大雪山，北至熱海、千泉，西至活國，東至烏鎩國，東西南北各數千里。崖嶺數百重，幽谷險峻，恒積氷雪，寒風勁烈。多出葱，故謂葱嶺；又以山崖葱翠，遂以名焉。
en_current: From here, traveling east, one enters the Congling (Onion Mountains). The Congling are situated in the center of Jambudvīpa; they connect to the Great Snow Mountains (大雪山) in the south, reach the Hot Sea (熱海) and the Thousand Springs (千泉) in the north, extend to the country of Huo (活國) in the west, and to the country of Wusha (烏鎩國) in the east. They extend for several thousand li in every direction. There are hundreds of layers of cliffs and ridges, with deep, precipitous valleys where ice and snow accumulate permanently and cold winds blow with great intensity. Because they produce many onions, they are called the Congling; furthermore, because the mountain cliffs are of an onion-green color, they are named accordingly.

zh: 東行百餘里，至瞢健國。瞢健國，覩貨邏國故地也。周四百餘里。國大都城周十五六里。土宜風俗，大同活國。無大君長，役屬突厥。
en_current: Traveling east for more than a hundred li, one reaches the country of Mungan (瞢健國). The country of Mungan is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is more than four hundred li in circuit. The capital city of the country is fifteen or sixteen li in circuit. The soil, products, and customs are much the same as those of the country of Hu (活國). There is no great sovereign, and it is subject to the Turks.

zh: 北至阿利尼國。阿利尼國，覩貨邏國故地也。帶縛芻河兩岸，周三百餘里。國大都城周十四五里。土宜風俗，大同活國。
en_current: To the north, one reaches the country of Alini (阿利尼國). The country of Alini is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It borders both banks of the Vaxšu River (縛芻河) and is over three hundred li in circuit. The capital city of the country is fourteen or fifteen li in circuit. The suitability of the soil and the customs are much the same as those of the country of Hu (活國).

zh: 東至曷邏胡國。曷邏胡國，覩貨邏國故地也。北臨縛芻河，周二百餘里。國大都城周十四五里。土宜風俗，大同活國。
en_current: To the east, one reaches the country of Rāhu (曷邏胡國). The country of Rāhu is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). To the north, it borders the Vaxšu River (縛芻河), and it is more than two hundred li in circuit. The capital city of the country is fourteen or fifteen li in circuit. The soil, products, and customs are much the same as those of the country of Hu (活國).

zh: 從瞢健國東踰峻嶺，越洞谷，歷數川城，行三百餘里，至訖栗瑟摩國。訖栗瑟摩國，覩貨邏國故地也。東西十餘里，南北三百餘里。國大都城周十五六里。土宜風俗，大同瞢健國，但其人性暴愚惡有異。
en_current: Going east from the country of Mungān (瞢健國), crossing steep mountain ranges, traversing deep valleys, and passing through several river cities for more than three hundred *li*, one reaches the country of Kṛṣma (訖栗瑟摩國). The country of Kṛṣma is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is more than ten *li* from east to west and three hundred *li* from north to south. The capital city of the country is fifteen or sixteen *li* in circumference. The native products and social customs are generally the same as those of the country of Mungān, but the people differ in being violent, foolish, and malicious in disposition.

zh: 北至鉢利曷國。鉢利曷國，覩貨邏國故地也。東西百餘里，南北三百餘里。國大都城周二十餘里。土宜風俗大同訖栗瑟摩國。
en_current: To the north lies the country of Parighar (鉢利曷國). The country of Parighar is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is over one hundred li from east to west and over three hundred li from south to north. The capital city of the country is over twenty li in circumference. The soil, products, and customs are much the same as those of the country of Kṛṣma (訖栗瑟摩國).

zh: 從訖栗瑟摩國東，踰山越川，行三百餘里，至呬摩呾羅國。呬摩呾羅國，覩貨邏國故地也。周三千餘里。山川邐迤，土地沃壤。宜穀稼，多宿麥，百卉滋茂，眾菓具繁。氣序寒烈，人性暴急，不識罪福，形貌鄙陋。舉措威儀，衣氈皮褐，頗同突厥。其婦人首冠木角，高三尺餘，前有兩岐，表夫父母；上岐表父，下岐表母，隨先喪亡，除去一岐，舅姑俱沒，角冠全棄。其先強國，王，釋種也，葱嶺之西，多見臣伏。境隣突厥，遂染其俗，又為侵掠，自守其境，故此國人，流離異域，數十堅城，各別立主，穹廬毳帳，遷徙往來。西接訖栗瑟摩國。
en_current: Going east from the country of Kṛṣma (訖栗瑟摩國), crossing mountains and traversing rivers for over three hundred li, one reaches the country of Himatala (呬摩呾羅國). The country of Himatala is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is over three thousand li in circumference. The mountains and rivers are winding and rugged, but the soil is fertile. It is suitable for grain crops, with an abundance of winter wheat; all kinds of plants grow luxuriantly, and various fruits are plentiful. The climate is cold and harsh. The people are violent and impetuous by nature, do not understand merit or sin, and their appearance is coarse and ugly. Their deportment and manners, as well as their clothing of felt and leather, are quite similar to those of the Turks. Their women wear wooden horns on their heads, over three feet high, with two branches in front representing their husband’s parents; the upper branch represents the father-in-law, and the lower branch represents the mother-in-law. As each passes away, the corresponding branch is removed; when both parents-in-law are deceased, the horn headdress is discarded entirely. In the past, this was a powerful kingdom, and the king was of the Śākya clan (釋種); to the west of the Onion Range (葱嶺), many states were subject to them. Because their borders neighbor the Turks, they have gradually adopted their customs; furthermore, due to being subjected to invasions and raids, they have had to defend their own territory. Consequently, the people of this country have been scattered into foreign lands, with dozens of fortified cities each having its own independent ruler, living in domed felt tents and moving about in search of pasture. To the west, it borders the country of Kṛṣma.

zh: 東谷行二百餘里，至鉢鐸創那國。鉢鐸創那國，覩貨邏國故地也。周二千餘里。國大都城據山崖上，周六七里。山川邐迤，沙石彌漫。土宜菽、麥，多蒱陶、胡桃、梨、柰等菓。氣序寒烈，人性剛猛。俗無禮法，不知學藝。其貌鄙陋，多衣氈褐。伽藍三四所，僧徒寡少。王性淳質，深信三寶。
en_current: Traveling east through the valley for more than two hundred *li*, one arrives at the country of Badakhshān (鉢鐸創那國). The country of Badakhshān is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is more than two thousand *li* in circuit. The capital city of the country is situated upon a mountain cliff and is six or seven *li* in circuit. The mountains and rivers are winding and rugged, and the land is filled with sand and stone. The soil is suitable for pulse and wheat, and there is an abundance of fruits such as grapes, walnuts, pears, and crabapples. The climate is cold and harsh, and the people are fierce and impetuous by nature. Their customs lack propriety and law, and they have no knowledge of the arts. Their appearance is coarse and ugly, and they mostly wear garments of felt and coarse wool. There are three or four *saṃghārāmas* (monasteries), with very few monks. The king is simple and honest by nature and has deep faith in the Three Jewels.

zh: 國大都城據山崖上，周六七里。
en_current: The capital city of the country (Bada-chuangna 鉢鐸創那國; Skt. Badakhshān) is situated upon a mountain cliff and is six or seven li in circuit.

zh: 從此東南，山谷中行二百餘里，至淫薄健國。淫薄健國，覩貨邏國故地也。周千餘里。國大都城周十餘里。山嶺連屬，川田隘狹。土地所產，氣序所宜，人性之差，同鉢鐸創那，但言語少異。王性苛暴，不明善惡。
en_current: From here, traveling southeast through a mountain valley for more than two hundred li, one reaches the country of Yambagan (淫薄健國). The country of Yambagan is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is more than one thousand li in circumference. The capital city of the country is more than ten li in circumference. The mountain ranges are connected, and the river valleys and fields are narrow and confined. The native products, the climate, and the character of the people are the same as those of Badakshān (鉢鐸創那), though the language is slightly different. The king is harsh and violent by nature, and he does not distinguish between good and evil.

zh: 從此東南，踰嶺越谷，峽路危險，行三百餘里，至屈（居勿反）浪拏國。屈浪拏國，覩貨邏國故地也。周二千餘里。土地山川，氣序時候，同淫薄健國。俗無法度，人性鄙暴。多不營福，少信佛法。其貌醜弊，多服氈褐。有山巖，中多出金精，琢析其石，然後得之。伽藍既少，僧徒亦寡。其王淳質，敬崇三寶。
en_current: From here, traveling southeast, crossing ridges and traversing valleys along dangerous canyon paths for more than three hundred li, one reaches the country of Kuraṇa (屈浪拏國) (屈 is pronounced by the *fanqie* 居勿). The country of Kuraṇa is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is more than two thousand li in circumference. The land, topography, and climate are the same as those of the country of Yambagan (淫薄健國). The customs lack laws and regulations, and the people’s nature is base and violent. Most do not cultivate merit, and few believe in the Buddha-Dharma. Their appearance is ugly and wretched, and they mostly wear felt and coarse wool. There are rocky mountains that produce much gold essence; one must chisel and break the stones to obtain it. The monasteries are few, and the monks are also scarce. Their king is simple and sincere, and he reveres and honors the Three Jewels.

zh: 從此東北，登山入谷，途路艱險，行五百餘里，至達摩悉鐵帝國（亦名鎮偘，又謂護蜜）。達摩悉鐵帝國，在兩山間，覩貨邏國故地也。東西千五六百餘里，南北廣四五里，狹則不踰一里。臨縛芻河，盤紆曲折，堆阜高下，沙石流漫，寒風淒烈。唯植麥、豆，少樹林，乏花菓。多出善馬，馬形雖小，而耐馳涉。俗無禮義，人性獷暴。形貌鄙陋，衣服氈褐。眼多碧綠，異於諸國。伽藍十餘所，僧徒寡少。
en_current: From here, traveling northeast, climbing mountains and entering valleys along a difficult and dangerous path for over five hundred li, one arrives at the country of Dharmasthiti (達摩悉鐵帝國) (also called Zhenkan [鎮偘], and also called Humi [護蜜]). The country of Dharmasthiti lies between two mountains and is the former territory of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國). It is over one thousand five or six hundred li from east to west, and four to five li wide from north to south, while at its narrowest it does not exceed one li. It borders the Vakṣu River (縛芻河), winding and twisting with uneven mounds and hillocks; sand and stones drift and spread, and the cold winds are harsh and piercing. They only plant wheat and beans; there are few forests and a lack of flowers and fruits. They produce many good horses; although the horses are small in stature, they are enduring in running and traveling. The customs lack propriety and righteousness, and the people’s nature is fierce and violent. Their appearance is base and ugly, and they wear felt and coarse wool garments. Their eyes are mostly emerald green, which is different from other countries. There are more than ten saṃghārāmas, but the number of monks is small.

zh: 昏馱多城，國之都也。中有伽藍，此國先王之所建立，疏崖奠谷，式建堂宇。此國之先，未被佛教，但事邪神，數百年前，肇弘法化。初，此國王愛子嬰疾，徒究醫術，有加無瘳。王乃躬往天祠，禮請求救。時彼祠主為神下語：「必當痊復，良無他慮。」王聞喜慰，回駕而歸。路逢沙門，容止可觀，駭其形服，問所從至。此沙門者，已證聖果，欲弘佛法，故此儀形。而報王曰：「我，如來弟子，所謂苾芻也。」王既憂心，即先問曰：「我子嬰疾，生死未分。」沙門曰：「王先靈可起，愛子難濟。」王曰：「天神謂其不死，沙門言其當終，詭俗之人，言何可信？」遲至宮中，愛子已死。匿不發喪，更問神主，猶曰：「不死，疹疾當瘳。」王便發怒，縛神主而數曰：「汝曹群居長惡，妄行威福。我子已死，尚云當瘳，此而謬惑，孰不可忍？宜戮神主，殄滅靈廟。」於是殺神主，除神像，投縛芻河。迴駕而還，又遇沙門，見而敬悅，稽首謝曰：「曩無明導，佇足邪途，澆弊雖久，沿革在茲，願能垂顧，降臨居室。」沙門受請，隨至中宮。葬子既已，謂沙門曰：「人世糺紛，生死流轉，我子嬰疾，問其去留，神而妄言，當必痊差。先承指告，果無虛說，斯則其法可奉，唯垂哀愍，導此迷徒。」遂請沙門揆度伽藍，依其規矩，而便建立。自爾之後，佛教方隆。故伽藍中精舍，為羅漢建也。伽藍大精舍中有石佛像，像上懸金銅圓蓋，眾寶莊嚴。人有旋繞，蓋亦隨轉，人止蓋止，莫測靈鑒。聞諸耆舊曰：或云聖人願力所持，或謂機關祕術所致。觀其堂宇，石壁堅峻。考厥眾議，莫知實錄。
en_current: The city of Khaṇḍata (昏馱多城) is the capital of the country. Within it is a monastery established by a former king of this country, who hollowed out the cliffs and filled the valleys to construct its halls and chambers. In earlier times, this country had not been reached by Buddhism and only worshipped heretical deities; it was only a few hundred years ago that the transformation of the Dharma began to spread.  Initially, the king’s beloved son fell ill. He exhausted all medical arts, but the illness only worsened without any sign of recovery. The king then went in person to a temple of the gods to offer rites and pray for salvation. At that time, the priest of the temple spoke on behalf of the deity: "He will certainly recover; there is truly no cause for concern." The king, hearing this, was joyful and comforted, and turned his carriage to return home. On the road, he encountered a śramaṇa whose demeanor was remarkable. Struck by his appearance and attire, the king asked where he had come from. This śramaṇa had already attained the holy fruit and, wishing to propagate the Buddha’s Dharma, had assumed this form. He replied to the king, "I am a disciple of the Tathāgata, what is known as a bhikṣu."  The king, being full of anxiety, immediately asked, "My son is afflicted with illness, and it is not yet certain whether he will live or die." The śramaṇa said, "The king’s ancestors may be raised, but your beloved son is difficult to save." The king said, "The heavenly deity said he would not die, yet this śramaṇa says he shall perish; how can the words of such a deceptive and vulgar man be trusted?"  Upon arriving at the palace, he found his beloved son had already died. He concealed the death and did not hold a funeral, instead asking the priest of the deity again, who still said, "He will not die; the illness will surely be cured." The king then flew into a rage, bound the priest, and rebuked him, saying, "You and your kind live together to foster evil, wantonly exercising power and claiming blessings." "My son is already dead, yet you still claim he will recover; such deceit and delusion are truly unbearable! It is fitting to execute the spirit-master and destroy the spirit-temple." Thereupon, he killed the spirit-master, removed the spirit-images, and cast them into the Vaxšu River (縛芻河). As he turned his carriage to return, he encountered a śramaṇa. Seeing him, he felt respect and joy, bowed his head, and apologized, saying, "In the past, I lacked a bright guide and lingered on evil paths. Although the corruption has lasted long, the reform begins here. I hope you will deign to look upon me and descend to my residence." The śramaṇa accepted the invitation and followed him to the inner palace. Once the son had been buried, the king said to the śramaṇa, "The human world is full of entanglement, and birth and death are in constant flux. When my son fell ill, I asked the spirit whether he would stay or depart, and the spirit spoke falsely, saying he would surely recover. Having previously received your instructions, which indeed proved not to be false, I see that your Dharma is worthy of devotion; I only pray that you will show compassion and guide this deluded follower." He then requested the śramaṇa to survey the site for a monastery (伽藍) and establish it according to the proper rules. From that time on, the Buddha's teaching flourished. Therefore, the vihāra (精舍) in the monastery was built for an arhat. In the great main hall of the monastery, there is a stone Buddha image, above which hangs a circular canopy of gilt bronze, adorned with various jewels. When people circumambulate, the canopy also rotates accordingly; when the people stop, the canopy stops. No one can fathom this spiritual manifestation. I heard from the elders that some say it is sustained by the power of a holy person's vow, while others say it is caused by secret mechanical arts. Observing the building, the stone walls are solid and steep. Examining all these opinions, no one knows the true account.

zh: 踰此國大山，北至尸棄尼國。尸棄尼國，周二千餘里。國大都城周五六里。山川連屬，沙石遍野。多宿、麥，少穀稼，林樹稀疎，花菓寡少。氣序寒烈，風俗獷勇，忍於殺戮，務於盜竊，不知禮義，不識善惡。迷未來禍福，懼現世災殃。形貌鄙陋，皮褐為服。文字同覩貨羅國，語言有異。
en_current: Crossing the great mountains of this country, one arrives north at the country of Šikni (尸棄尼國). The country of Šikni is over two thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is five or six li in circuit. The mountains and rivers are connected, and the fields are covered with sand and stone. There is much winter wheat, but few cereal crops; trees are sparse, and flowers and fruits are scarce. The climate is bitterly cold. The customs of the people are fierce and brave; they are hardened to slaughter and devoted to theft. They do not know ritual or righteousness, and they do not distinguish between good and evil. They are confused about future misfortune or blessings, yet they fear the calamities of the present life. Their appearance is coarse and unsightly, and they wear skins and coarse wool for clothing. Their writing is the same as that of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨羅國), but their spoken language is different.

zh: 尸棄尼國，周二千餘里。國大都城周五六里。
en_current: The country of Śiknī (尸棄尼國) is over two thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is five or six li in circuit.

zh: 越達摩悉鐵帝國大山之南，至商彌國。商彌國，周二千五六百里。山川相間，堆阜高下。穀稼備植，菽、麥彌豐，多蒱陶，出雌黃，鑿崖析石，然後得之。山神暴惡，屢為災害，祀祭後入，平吉往來。若不祈禱，風雹奮發。氣序寒，風俗急。人性淳質，俗無禮義，智謀寡狹，伎能淺薄。文字同覩貨邏國，語言別異。多衣氈褐。其王，釋種也，崇重佛法，國人從化，莫不淳信。伽藍二所，僧徒寡少。
en_current: Crossing to the south of the great mountains of the country of Dharmasthiti (達摩悉鐵帝國), one arrives at the country of Śami (商彌國). The country of Śami is two thousand five or six hundred li in circumference. Mountains and rivers alternate, with high and low hills interspersed. All kinds of grain are planted, with pulse and wheat being particularly abundant; there are many grapes, and the land produces orpiment, which is obtained by splitting the rocks hewn from the cliffs. The mountain gods are fierce and malicious, repeatedly causing calamities; only after offering sacrifices can one enter, and then travel back and forth in safety. If one does not pray, winds and hail break out. The climate is cold, and the customs are impetuous. The people are simple and honest in disposition, but their customs lack etiquette and righteousness; their wisdom is limited, and their skills are superficial. Their script is the same as that of the country of Tukhāra (覩貨邏國), but their spoken language is different. They mostly wear felt and coarse wool garments. Their king is of the Śākya clan and deeply reveres the Buddha's teachings; the people follow his example, and all are pure in their faith. There are two saṃghārāmas, with few monks.

zh: 國境東北，踰山越谷，經危履險，行七百餘里，至波謎羅川。東西千餘里，南北百餘里，狹隘之處不踰十里。據兩雪山間，故寒風凄勁，春夏飛雪，晝夜飄風。地鹹鹵，多礫石，播植不滋，草木稀少，遂致空荒，絕無人止。
en_current: To the northeast of the country, crossing mountains and traversing valleys, passing through dangerous terrain and treading over perilous paths for over seven hundred li, one arrives at the Pamir Valley (波謎羅川). It extends over one thousand li from east to west and over one hundred li from south to north, while at its narrowest point it is no more than ten li wide. It is situated between two snowy mountains, and therefore the cold winds are piercingly strong; snow falls during the spring and summer, and winds swirl day and night. The soil is saline and alkaline, with much gravel and stone; crops do not flourish, and vegetation is sparse, which leads to it being a desolate wilderness, entirely devoid of human habitation.

zh: 波謎羅川中有大龍池，東西三百餘里，南北五十餘里，據大葱嶺內，當贍部洲中，其地最高也。水乃澄清皎鏡，莫測其深，色帶青黑，味甚甘美。潛居則鮫、螭、魚、龍、黿、鼉、龜、鼈，浮游乃鴛鴦、鴻雁、鴐鵝、鷫、鳵，諸鳥太卵，遺㲉荒野，或草澤間，或沙渚上。池西派一大流，西至達摩悉鐵帝國東界，與縛芻河合而西流，故此已右，水皆西流。池東派一大流，東北至佉沙國西界，與徙多河合而東流，故此已左，水皆東流。波謎羅川南越山，有鉢露羅國，多金、銀，金色如火。
en_current: In the Pamir (波謎羅) Valley lies the Great Dragon Lake, extending over three hundred *li* from east to west and over fifty *li* from north to south. It is situated within the Great Onion Range (大葱嶺), lies at the center of Jambudvīpa (贍部洲), and occupies the highest elevation. The water is clear and bright as a mirror, its depth unfathomable, its color a dark blue-black, and its taste extremely sweet. Submerged within it dwell sharks, *chi*-dragons, fish, dragons, soft-shelled turtles, alligators, tortoises, and turtles. Floating and swimming upon it are mandarin ducks, wild geese, *jia*-geese, *su*-birds, and *hu*-birds. These birds lay large eggs, leaving their shells in the wilderness, either among the grassy marshes or upon the sandy islets. A large stream flows out from the west of the lake, running west to the eastern boundary of the Dharmasthiti (達摩悉鐵帝) country, where it joins the Vakṣu (縛芻) River and flows westward; therefore, to the right of this point, all waters flow to the west. A large stream flows out from the east of the lake, running northeast to the western boundary of the Khāsa (佉沙) country, where it joins the Sītā (徙多) River and flows eastward; therefore, to the left of this point, all waters flow to the east. South of the Pamir Valley, crossing the mountains, is the Balūra (鉢露羅) country, which abounds in gold and silver; the color of the gold is like fire.

zh: 自此川中東南，登山履險，路無人里，唯多氷雪。行五百餘里，至朅盤陀國。朅盤陀國，周二千餘里。國大都城基大石嶺，背徙多河，周二十餘里。山嶺連屬，川原隘狹。穀稼儉少，菽、麥豐多，林樹稀，花菓少。原隰丘墟，城邑空曠。俗無禮義，人寡學藝。性既獷暴，力亦驍勇。容貌醜弊，衣服氈褐。文字、語言，大同佉沙國。然知淳信，敬崇佛法。伽藍十餘所，僧徒五百餘人，習學小乘教說一切有部。今王淳質，敬重三寶，儀容閑雅，篤志好學。建國已來，多歷年所。其自稱云是至那提婆瞿呾羅（唐言漢日天種）。此國之先，葱嶺中荒川也。昔波利剌斯國王娶婦漢土，迎歸至此，時屬兵亂，東西路絕，遂以王女置於孤峯，極危峻，梯崖而上下，設周衛警，晝巡夜。時經三月，寇賊方靜，欲趣歸路，女已有娠。使臣惶懼，謂徒屬曰：「王命迎婦，屬斯寇亂，野次荒川，朝不謀夕。吾王德感，妖氛已靜，今將歸國，王婦有娠。顧此為憂，不知死地，宜推首惡，或以後誅。」訊問諠譁，莫究其實。時彼侍兒謂使臣曰：「勿相尤也，乃神會耳。每日正中，有一丈夫從日輪中乘馬會此。」使臣曰：「若然者，何以雪罪？歸必見誅，留亦來討，進退若是，何所宜行？」僉曰：「斯事不細，誰就深誅？待罪境外，且推旦夕。」於是即石峯上築宮起館，周三百餘步。環宮築城，立女為主，建官垂憲。至期產男，容貌妍麗。母攝政事，子稱尊號。飛行虛空，控馭風雲，威德遐被，聲教遠洽，隣域異國，莫不稱臣。其王壽終，葬在此城東南百餘里大山巖石室中。其屍乾腊，今猶不壞，狀羸瘠人，儼然如睡，時易衣服，恒置香花。子孫奕世以迄于今。以其先祖之世，母則漢土之人，父乃日天之種，故其自稱漢日天種。然其王族，貌同中國，首飾方冠，身衣胡服。後嗣陵夷，見迫強國。無憂王命世，即其宮中建窣堵波。其王於後遷居宮東北隅，以其故宮，為尊者童受論師建僧伽藍，臺閣高廣，佛像威嚴。尊者，呾叉始羅國人也，幼而穎悟，早離俗塵，遊心典籍，棲神玄旨，日誦三萬二千言，兼書三萬二千字。故能學冠時彥，名高當世，立正法，摧邪見，高論清舉，無難不酬，五印度國咸見推高。其所製論凡數十部，並盛宣行，莫不翫習，即經部本師也。當此之時，東有馬鳴，南有提婆，西有龍猛，北有童受，號為四日照世。故此國王聞尊者盛德，興兵動眾，伐呾叉始羅國，脇而得之，建此伽藍，式昭瞻仰。
en_current: From this valley, traveling southeast, one climbs mountains and traverses dangerous paths where there are no human habitations, only much ice and snow. After traveling more than five hundred li, one reaches the country of Kharbanda (朅盤陀國). The country of Kharbanda is over two thousand li in circuit. The capital city is built upon a large rocky ridge, with the Sītā River (徙多河) at its back, and it is over twenty li in circuit. The mountain ranges are connected, and the valleys and plains are narrow. Grain crops are scarce, but beans and wheat are abundant; trees are sparse, and there is little fruit or flowers. The plains and marshes are desolate, and the cities and towns are empty. The customs lack propriety and righteousness, and the people have little learning or skill. Their nature is fierce and violent, yet they are also brave and valiant. Their appearance is ugly and wretched, and they wear garments of felt and coarse wool. Their script and language are largely the same as those of the country of Khāsa (佉沙國). However, they are sincere in their faith and deeply revere the Buddhadharma. There are more than ten monasteries and over five hundred monks, who study the teachings of the Small Vehicle (Hīnayāna) according to the Sarvāstivāda school. The current king is simple and honest, respects the Three Jewels, is refined and elegant in his demeanor, and is devoted to learning. Since the founding of the kingdom, many years have passed. The people claim to be the descendants of the *Cīna-deva-gotra* (至那提婆瞿呾羅) (in the language of the Tang, "the race of the Han and the Sun-deva"). The origin of this country was a desolate valley in the Onion Range (Pamirs). Long ago, a king of Persia (波利剌斯) married a princess from the land of Han and was escorting her back when they reached this place. At that time, there was a military rebellion, and the roads to the east and west were blocked. He therefore placed the princess upon an isolated peak, which was extremely steep and dangerous, accessible only by ladders to ascend or descend, and he stationed guards all around to keep watch day and night. Three months passed, and the bandits were finally pacified. When he intended to continue on the road home, the princess was already pregnant. The envoy was terrified and said to his retinue, "The King ordered us to welcome his bride, but we encountered this rebellion; camping in the wild barrens, we cannot even plan for the next morning. Through the virtue of our King, the baleful atmosphere has been cleared, and now we are to return to the kingdom, yet the King’s bride is pregnant. Considering this, we are in distress, not knowing where I shall die; we should seek out the chief culprit, so that he may be executed afterwards." There was a clamor of questioning, but no one could determine the truth. At that time, a maidservant said to the envoy, "Do not blame one another; it was a divine encounter. Every day at high noon, a man would arrive here on horseback, descending from the solar disc." The envoy said, "If that is the case, how can we clear ourselves of this guilt? If we return, we will surely be executed; if we stay, we will also be punished. With advancement or retreat being thus, what is the proper course of action?" They all agreed, "This matter is not trivial; who would willingly face such severe punishment? Let us await our fate outside the borders and delay for a while."  Thereupon, they built a palace and quarters on the stone peak, with a circumference of more than three hundred paces. They built a city wall around the palace, established the woman as sovereign, and instituted officials and laws. When the time came, she gave birth to a son, whose appearance was beautiful and refined. The mother managed the affairs of state, and the son assumed the royal title. He could fly through the void and control the wind and clouds; his majesty and virtue reached far and wide, and his reputation and teachings spread to distant lands. Neighboring regions and foreign countries all paid him homage. When the king died at a ripe old age, he was buried in a stone chamber within a large mountain over a hundred *li* southeast of this city. His corpse was preserved like a mummy and remains intact to this day; resembling an emaciated person, he looks as if he were fast asleep, and his clothes are changed periodically while incense and flowers are constantly placed before him. His descendants have continued through the generations down to the present day. Because in the time of their ancestor, the mother was a person from the land of Han (China) and the father was of the seed of the Sun God, they call themselves the "Han-Sun-God Clan." However, their royal family resembles the people of the Middle Kingdom (China) in appearance; they wear square crowns as head ornaments and dress in foreign clothing. Later, their descendants declined and were pressured by powerful states. King Aśoka (無憂王) appeared in the world and built a stupa within their palace. The king later moved his residence to the northeast corner of the palace and converted his former palace into a monastery for the venerable Shastra Master Kumāralāta (童受論師), with lofty, spacious terraces and pavilions and solemn, majestic Buddha statues. The venerable master was a native of the country of Takṣaśilā (呾叉始羅國); he was brilliant from childhood, renounced the secular world early, devoted his mind to the scriptures, and focused his spirit on the profound mysteries, daily reciting thirty-two thousand words and writing another thirty-two thousand. Thus, his learning surpassed the scholars of his time, and his fame was high in the world; he established the True Dharma, refuted heterodox views, and his lofty discourses were clear and elevated, leaving no difficulty unaddressed, so that he was universally esteemed throughout the five Indias. The treatises he authored number several dozen; they are all widely circulated and studied, for he is the founding master of the Sautrāntika school. At that time, there was Aśvaghoṣa in the east, Deva in the south, Nāgārjuna in the west, and Kumāralāta in the north; they were known as the "four suns that illuminate the world." Therefore, the king of this country, having heard of the venerable master's great virtue, mobilized his troops to attack the country of Takṣaśilā and obtained him by coercion; he then built this monastery to manifest his reverence.

zh: 昔波利剌斯國王娶婦漢土，迎歸至此，時屬兵亂，東西路絕，遂以王女置於孤峯，極危峻，梯崖而上下，設周衛警，晝巡夜。時經三月，寇賊方靜，欲趣歸路，女已有娠。使臣惶懼，謂徒屬曰：「王命迎婦，屬斯寇亂，野次荒川，朝不謀夕。吾王德感，妖氛已靜，今將歸國，王婦有娠。顧此為憂，不知死地，宜推首惡，或以後誅。」訊問諠譁，莫究其實。時彼侍兒謂使臣曰：「勿相尤也，乃神會耳。每日正中，有一丈夫從日輪中乘馬會此。」使臣曰：「若然者，何以雪罪？歸必見誅，留亦來討，進退若是，何所宜行？」僉曰：「斯事不細，誰就深誅？待罪境外，且推旦夕。」於是即石峯上築宮起館，周三百餘步。環宮築城，立女為主，建官垂憲。
en_current: Long ago, a king of Persia (波利剌斯國) married a wife from the land of Han. While escorting her back, they reached this place, but at that time there was a military rebellion, and the roads to the east and west were cut off. Consequently, they placed the king’s wife upon an isolated peak, which was extremely steep and precipitous; one had to use ladders to ascend or descend, and they established guards all around to keep watch day and night. Three months passed, and the bandits were finally pacified. They intended to proceed on the road home, but the woman was already pregnant. The envoy was terrified and said to his subordinates, "The King ordered us to welcome his bride, but we encountered this rebellion, camping in the wild barrens, unable to plan for the next morning. Through our King’s virtuous influence, the evil aura has been quelled, and now that we are about to return to our country, the King’s bride is pregnant. Considering this, it is a source of anxiety; we do not know if we will die here. We should identify the ringleader and perhaps execute him later." The questioning and clamor were loud, but they could not determine the truth. At that time, her maidservant said to the envoy, "Do not blame one another; it was a divine encounter. Every day at high noon, a man descends from the solar disc riding a horse to meet her here." The envoy said, "If that is the case, how can we clear ourselves of this guilt? If we return, we will surely be executed; if we stay, we will also be punished. With such a dilemma, what should we do?" They all agreed, "This matter is not trivial; who would willingly accept a severe execution? Let us await our punishment outside the borders and delay the matter for a while." Thereupon, they built a palace and quarters on the stone peak, with a circumference of more than three hundred paces. They built a city wall around the palace, established the woman as the ruler, and appointed officials to establish laws.

zh: 城東南行三百餘里，至大石崖，有二石室，各一羅漢於中入滅盡定。端然而坐，難以動搖，形若羸人，膚骸不朽，已經七百餘歲，其鬚髮恒長，故眾僧年別為剃髮易衣。
en_current: Traveling three hundred-odd *li* to the southeast of the city, one reaches a great rocky cliff where there are two stone chambers, in each of which an Arhat (阿羅漢) has entered the samādhi of extinction (滅盡定). They sit upright and are difficult to move; their forms resemble those of emaciated men, yet their skin and bones have not decayed, having already remained so for over seven hundred years. Their hair and beards grow constantly, and for this reason, the monks shave them and change their robes every year.

zh: 大崖東北，踰嶺履險，行二百餘里，至奔（通論反）穰舍羅（唐言福舍）。葱嶺東岡，四山之中，地方百餘頃，正中墊下。冬夏積雪，風寒飄勁。疇壟舃鹵，稼穡不滋，既無林樹，唯有細草。時雖暑熱，而多風雪，人徒纔入，雲霧已興，商侶往來，苦斯艱險。聞諸耆舊曰：昔有賈客，其徒萬餘，槖駝數千，齎貨逐利，遭風遇雪，人畜俱喪。時朅盤陀國有大羅漢，遙觀見之，愍其危厄，欲運神通，拯斯淪溺；適來至此，商人已喪。於是收諸珍寶，集其所有，構立館舍，儲積資財，買地隣國，鬻戶邊城，以賑往來。故今行人商侶，咸蒙周給。
en_current: To the northeast of the great cliff, crossing ridges and traversing dangerous paths for over two hundred *li*, one arrives at Puṇyaśālā (奔穰舍羅) (奔 is pronounced by the *fanqie* 通論; in the Tang language, "House of Merit"). It is situated on the eastern ridge of the Onion Range (葱嶺), amidst four mountains, in a basin over one hundred *qing* in area, sunken in the center. Snow accumulates there throughout winter and summer, and the wind is cold and fierce. The fields and ridges are saline and barren, so crops do not grow; there are no trees, only fine grass. Even during the heat of summer, there is much wind and snow; as soon as travelers enter, clouds and mist arise, and merchant caravans suffer greatly from these hardships and dangers.  I have heard from the elders: once there were merchants with a following of over ten thousand and several thousand camels, carrying goods in pursuit of profit, who encountered wind and snow, and both people and animals perished. At that time, there was a great Arhat in the kingdom of *Kharbanda* (朅盤陀國) who saw them from afar; pitying their peril, he desired to exercise his supernatural powers to rescue them from their plight, but by the time he arrived, the merchants had already perished. He then collected their various treasures, gathered all that remained, constructed a building, stored up provisions, purchased land in neighboring countries, and bought households in border cities to provide relief for those traveling to and fro. Therefore, travelers and merchant caravans today all receive support from this.

zh: 從此東下葱嶺東岡，登危嶺，越洞谷，谿徑險阻，風雪相繼，行八百餘里，出葱嶺，至烏鎩國。烏鎩國，周千餘里。國大都城周十餘里，南臨徙多河。地土沃壤，稼穡殷盛，林樹欝茂，花菓具繁。多出雜玉，則有白玉、黳玉、青玉。氣序和，風雨順。俗寡禮義，人性剛獷，多詭詐，少廉恥。文字、語言少同佉沙國。容貌醜弊，衣服皮褐。然能崇信敬奉佛法。伽藍十餘所，僧徒減千人，習學小乘教說一切有部。自數百年，王族絕嗣，無別君長，役屬朅盤陀國。
en_current: From this point, going eastward down the eastern ridges of the Pamir Mountains (葱嶺), climbing perilous peaks and crossing deep valleys, through dangerous mountain paths and amid continuous wind and snow, I traveled over eight hundred li, emerged from the Pamirs, and reached the kingdom of Wusha (烏鎩國). The kingdom of Wusha is over one thousand li in circuit. The capital city is over ten li in circuit and borders the Sītā River (徙多河) to the south. The soil is rich and fertile, crops are abundant, forests are lush, and flowers and fruits are plentiful. The land produces much variegated jade, including white jade, black jade, and green jade. The climate is temperate, and the wind and rain are timely. The customs lack propriety and righteousness; the people are by nature stubborn and fierce, prone to deceit, and lacking in shame. Their writing and language are somewhat similar to those of the kingdom of Khāsa (佉沙國). Their appearance is unsightly, and they wear garments of leather and wool. Nevertheless, they are able to revere and serve the Buddhadharma. There are more than ten saṃghārāmas, with fewer than one thousand monks, who study the teachings of the Small Vehicle according to the Sarvāstivāda school. For several hundred years, the royal line has been extinct, and having no separate ruler, they are subject to the kingdom of Kharbanda (朅盤陀國).

zh: 城西二百餘里，至大山。山氣巃嵸，觸石興雲，崖隒崢嶸，將崩未墜。其巔窣堵波，欝然奇制也。聞諸土俗曰：數百年前，山崖崩圮，中有苾芻，瞑目而坐，軀量偉大，形容枯槁，鬚髮下垂，被肩蒙面。有田獵者見已白王，王躬觀禮。都人士子，不召而至，焚香散花，競修供養。王曰：「斯何人哉？若此偉也！」有苾芻對曰：「此鬚髮垂長而被服袈裟，乃入滅心定阿羅漢也。夫入滅心定者，先有期限，或言聞揵稚聲，或言待日光照，有茲警察，便從定起；若無警察，寂然不動，定力持身，遂無壞滅。段食之體，出定便謝。宜以蘇油灌注，令得滋潤，然後鼓擊，警悟定心。」王曰：「俞乎？」乃擊揵稚。其聲纔振，而此羅漢豁然高視，久之，乃曰：「爾輩何人？形容卑劣，被服袈裟？」對曰：「我苾芻也。」曰：「然，我師迦葉波如來今何所在？」對曰：「入大涅槃，其來已久。」聞而閉目，悵若有懷，尋重問曰：「釋迦如來出興世耶？」對曰：「誕靈導世，已從寂滅。」聞復俯首，久之乃起，昇虛空，現神變，化火焚身，遺骸墜地。王收其骨起窣堵波。
en_current: Two hundred or more *li* west of the city, one arrives at a great mountain. The mountain’s atmosphere is dense and swirling; clouds rise where it touches the rocks, and the cliffs and precipices are jagged and steep, as if about to collapse yet not falling. On its summit is a stūpa of imposing and extraordinary construction. According to local tradition, several hundred years ago, a mountain cliff collapsed, and within it was a bhikṣu sitting with eyes closed. His body was of great stature, his appearance emaciated, and his beard and hair hung down, covering his shoulders and face. A hunter saw him and reported it to the king, who went in person to pay his respects. The city’s inhabitants and scholars arrived without being summoned, burning incense and scattering flowers, vying to offer worship. The king asked, "Who is this person? He is so magnificent!" A bhikṣu replied, "This person with long, hanging hair and beard, clad in a kaṣāya robe, is an arhat who has entered the samādhi of mental extinction (nirodha-samāpatti). Those who enter the samādhi of mental extinction set a prior time limit; some say they will arise upon hearing the sound of a ghaṇṭā, others say they will wait for the sunlight to shine. With such an alert, they arise from their meditation; if there is no alert, they remain silent and motionless, the power of their meditation sustaining their body so that it does not decay. The physical body, sustained by morsel food, would perish upon emerging from meditation. It is proper to pour in ghee to provide nourishment and moisture, and only then strike the ghaṇṭā to awaken his meditative mind." The king said, "Is that so?" He then struck the ghaṇṭā. The sound had barely vibrated when the arhat suddenly opened his eyes and looked up. After a long while, he said, "Who are you people? Your appearance is base and inferior, yet you wear the kaṣāya robes?" They replied, "We are bhikṣus." He asked, "Is that so? Where is my teacher, Kāśyapa Tathāgata (迦葉波如來), now?" They replied, "He entered mahānirvāṇa a long time ago." Upon hearing this, he closed his eyes, looking dejected as if lost in thought. Shortly after, he asked again, "Has Śākya Tathāgata (釋迦如來) appeared in the world?" They replied, "The holy one who guided the world has already passed into extinction." Hearing this, he bowed his head again, and after a long while, he rose, ascended into the void, manifested supernatural transformations, and transformed into fire to consume his body, his remains falling to the ground. The king collected his bones and erected a stūpa (窣堵波) over them.

zh: 從此北行，山磧曠野五百餘里，至佉沙國（舊謂疏勒者，乃稱其城號也。正音宜云室利訖栗多底。疏勒之言，猶為訛也）。佉沙國，周五千餘里。多沙磧，少壤土。稼穡殷盛，花菓繁茂。出細氈褐，工織細㲲氍毺。氣候和暢，風雨順序。人性獷暴，俗多詭詐，禮義輕薄，學藝膚淺。其俗生子，押頭匾㔸，容貌麁鄙，文身綠睛。而其文字，取則印度，雖有刪訛，頗存體勢。語言辭調，異於諸國。淳信佛法，勤營福利。伽藍數百所，僧徒萬餘人，習學小乘教說一切有部。不究其理，多諷其文，故誦通三藏及《毘婆沙》者多矣。
en_current: Traveling north from here for over five hundred li across mountains, gravelly plains, and wilderness, one arrives at the country of Khāsa (佉沙國) (What was formerly called Shule (疏勒) is actually the name of its capital city. The correct pronunciation should be Śrī-kṛtati; the term Shule is a corruption). The country of Khāsa is over five thousand li in circumference. There is much gravel and sand, and little fertile soil. Agriculture is flourishing, and flowers and fruits are abundant. It produces fine felt and coarse wool, and they are skilled at weaving fine cotton cloth and woollen rugs. The climate is mild and pleasant, and the winds and rains follow their proper seasons. The people are fierce and violent by nature, and their customs are full of deceit; they treat ritual and righteousness lightly, and their learning and arts are superficial. It is their custom to compress the heads of newborn children to make them flat; their appearance is coarse and vulgar, and they have tattooed bodies and green eyes. Their writing system is modeled after that of India; although there have been deletions and corruptions, it still retains the original structure. Their language and tone of speech differ from those of other countries. They are sincerely devoted to the Buddha-dharma and diligently engage in meritorious works. There are several hundred saṃghārāmas with over ten thousand monks, who study the Lesser Vehicle (Hīnayāna) teachings of the Sarvāstivāda school. They do not delve deeply into the principles but mostly recite the texts; therefore, many have mastered the recitation of the Tripiṭaka and the Mahāvibhāṣā-śāstra.

zh: 從此東南行五百餘里，濟徙多河，踰大沙嶺，至斫句迦國（舊曰沮渠）。斫句迦國，周千餘里。國大都城周十餘里，堅峻險固，編戶殷盛。山阜連屬，礫石彌漫，臨帶兩河，頗以耕植。蒲陶、梨、柰，其菓寔繁。時風寒，人躁暴。俗唯詭詐，公行劫盜。文字同瞿薩旦那國，言語有異。禮義輕薄，學藝淺近。淳信三寶，好樂福利。伽藍數十，毀壞已多，僧徒百餘人，習學大乘教。
en_current: From here, traveling southeast for more than five hundred li, I crossed the Sītā River, passed over a great sandy range, and reached the country of Cukuka (formerly called Juqu). The country of Cukuka is more than one thousand li in circuit. The capital city of the country is more than ten li in circuit; it is solid, steep, and secure, and the households are numerous and prosperous. The hills and mounds are connected, and the ground is covered with gravel and stones. It borders two rivers and is quite suitable for cultivation. Grapes, pears, and crabapples—these fruits are abundant. The climate is cold, and the people are impetuous and violent. Their customs are characterized by deceit and trickery, and they practice robbery openly. Their script is the same as that of the country of Gostāna (瞿薩旦那國), though their spoken language is different. Their sense of propriety and righteousness is slight, and their learning and arts are shallow. They are sincerely devoted to the Three Jewels and take pleasure in performing meritorious deeds. There are several dozen sanghārāmas, though many are in ruins, and there are more than one hundred monks who study the teachings of the Great Vehicle.

zh: 國南境有大山，崖嶺嵯峨，峯巒重疊；草木凌寒，春秋一觀；谿㵎浚瀨，飛流四注；崖龕石室，棋布巖林。印度果人，多運神通，輕舉遠遊，棲止於此。諸阿羅漢寂滅者眾，以故多有窣堵波也，今猶現有三阿羅漢居巖穴中，入滅心定，形若羸人，鬚髮恒長，故諸沙門時往為剃。而此國中大乘經典部數尤多，佛法至處，莫斯為盛也。十萬頌為部者，凡有十數；自茲已降，其流寔廣。
en_current: On the southern border of the country is a great mountain, with craggy cliffs and ridges and overlapping peaks. The vegetation defies the cold, looking the same in spring and autumn. Deep ravines and rushing torrents flow in all directions, and cliff niches and stone chambers are scattered like chess pieces throughout the rocky forests. Many people from India who have attained the fruits of enlightenment employ their supernatural powers to travel far and alight here to dwell. Because many Arhats have entered nirvana here, there are numerous stupas. Even now, three Arhats remain in the mountain caves, having entered the samadhi of mental extinction; their forms appear like those of emaciated men, and their hair and beards grow continuously, so monks periodically go there to shave them. In this country, the number of Mahayana scriptures is particularly large; of all the places where the Buddha’s teachings have spread, none is more flourishing than this. There are over ten works consisting of one hundred thousand stanzas each, and from this size on down, their circulation is truly vast.

zh: 從此而東，踰嶺越谷，行八百餘里，至瞿薩旦那國（唐言地乳，即其俗之雅言也。俗語謂之渙那國，匈奴謂之于遁，諸胡謂之谿旦，印度謂之屈丹。舊曰于闐，訛也）。瞿薩旦那國，周四千餘里。沙磧太半，壤土隘狹。宜穀稼，多眾菓。出氍毺、細氈，工紡績絁紬。又產白玉、黳玉。氣序和暢，飄風飛埃。俗知禮義，人性溫恭。好學典藝，博達技能。眾庶富樂，編戶安業。國尚樂音，人好歌舞。少服毛褐氈裘，多衣絁紬白㲲。儀形有禮，風則有紀。文字憲章，聿尊印度，微改體勢，粗有沿革。語異諸國。崇尚佛法。伽藍百有餘所，僧徒五千餘人，並多習學大乘法教。王甚驍武，敬重佛法，自云毘沙門天之祚胤也。昔者，此國虛曠無人，毘沙門天於此棲止。無憂王太子在呾叉始羅國被抉目已，無憂王怒譴輔佐，遷其豪族，出雪山北，居荒谷間。遷人逐物，至此西界，推舉酋豪，尊立為王。當是時也，東土帝子蒙譴流徙，居此東界，群下勸進，又自稱王。歲月已積，風教不通。各因田獵，遇會荒澤，更問宗緒，因而爭長。忿形辭語，便欲交兵。或有諫曰：「今何遽乎？因獵決戰，未盡兵鋒。宜歸治兵，期而後集。」於是迴駕而返，各歸其國，校習戎馬，督勵士卒。至期兵會，旗鼓相望。旦日合戰，西主不利，因而逐北，遂斬其首。東主乘勝，撫集亡國，遷都中地，方建城郭。憂其無土，恐難成功，宣告遠近，誰識地理。時有塗灰外道，負大瓠，盛滿水，而自進曰：「我知地理。」遂以其水屈曲遺流，周而復始，因即疾驅，忽而不見。依彼水迹，峙其基堵，遂得興功，即斯國治，今王所都於此城也。城非崇峻，攻擊難剋，自古已來，未能有勝。其王遷都作邑，建國安人，功績已成，齒耋云暮，未有胤嗣，恐絕宗緒。乃往毘沙門天神所祈禱請嗣，神像額上，剖出嬰孩，捧以回駕，國人稱慶。既不飲乳，恐其不壽，尋詣神祠，重請育養。神前之地忽然隆起，其狀如乳，神童飲吮，遂至成立。智勇光前，風教遐被，遂營神祠，宗先祖也。自茲已降，奕世相承，傳國君臨，不失其緒。故今神廟多諸珍寶，拜祠享祭，無替於時。地乳所育，因為國號。
en_current: Going eastward from here, crossing mountains and valleys for more than eight hundred li, one reaches the country of Gostana (瞿薩旦那國) (in the language of Tang, this means "Earth-Nipple," which is the elegant form of the local name. In the vulgar tongue it is called the country of Huanna; the Xiongnu call it Yudun; the various Hu peoples call it Qidan; and in India it is called Qudan. The old name, Yutian (于闐), is erroneous). The country of Gostana is more than four thousand li in circumference. More than half of it is sand and gravel, and the arable land is narrow and restricted. It is suitable for grain crops and produces many kinds of fruit. It produces rugs and fine felt, and the people are skilled at spinning and weaving silk and pongee. It also produces white jade and black jade. The climate is mild and pleasant, though there are drifting winds and flying dust. The customs value propriety and righteousness, and the people are gentle and respectful by nature. They are fond of learning the arts and are broadly proficient in various skills. The populace is wealthy and happy, and the households are settled in their occupations. The country prizes musical sounds, and the people are fond of singing and dancing. Few wear coarse wool, felt, or furs; most clothe themselves in silk, pongee, and white cotton. Their deportment is refined, and their customs are well-ordered. Their writing and laws are modeled after those of India, though they have slightly altered the style and form, having undergone some evolution. Their language differs from that of other countries. They revere and uphold the Buddha-dharma. There are more than one hundred sanghārāmas (伽藍) and over five thousand monks, most of whom study the teachings of the Mahāyāna. The king is very brave and martial, respects the Buddha-dharma, and claims to be a descendant of the deity Vaiśravaṇa (毘沙門天). In ancient times, this country was empty and uninhabited, and the deity Vaiśravaṇa resided here. After the crown prince of King Aśoka (無憂王) had his eyes gouged out in the country of Takṣaśilā (呾叉始羅國), the king angrily rebuked his ministers and exiled the powerful families to the north of the Snow Mountains to dwell among the desolate valleys. These exiles followed their herds and reached the western border of this land, where they elected their leader and established him as king. At that time, a prince from the eastern lands had been banished and had migrated to dwell on the eastern border of this region; his subordinates urged him to assume the throne, and he too proclaimed himself king. As years and months accumulated, their customs and teachings remained disconnected. Each group, while out hunting, encountered the other in the desolate marshes; they inquired about each other’s lineage and consequently disputed who was superior. Anger manifested in their words, and they were about to engage in battle. Someone advised them, saying, "Why be so hasty now? To decide the battle while hunting does not fully display the sharpness of our weapons. It is better to return and prepare our troops, and gather at an appointed time." Thereupon, they turned their carriages and returned, each going back to his own country to drill their horses and soldiers and encourage their troops. When the appointed time arrived, the armies met, and their banners and drums faced one another. The next day they joined battle, and the Western Lord was disadvantaged; consequently, he was pursued in his retreat and his head was cut off. The Eastern Lord, riding the momentum of his victory, pacified and gathered the people of the defeated country, moved his capital to the central region, and began to build city walls. Worried that he lacked land and fearing that he might not succeed, he made a proclamation far and near, asking who knew the geography. At that time, there was an ash-smeared outsider (tīrthika) who carried a large gourd filled with water and stepped forward, saying, "I know the geography." He then let the water flow out in winding curves, returning to where it started, and then he hurried away and suddenly vanished. Following those water marks, the foundations were raised and the construction was successfully completed; this became the seat of government, and it is in this city that the current king has established his capital. The city is not high or steep, yet it is difficult to overcome by attack, and from ancient times until now, no one has been able to conquer it. By the time the king had moved the capital to build this city, established the state, and settled the people, his achievements were complete and he was in the twilight of his old age; yet he had no heir and feared the end of his ancestral line. He then went to the place of the god Vaiśravaṇa (毘沙門天神) to pray for an heir. From the forehead of the god’s statue, an infant was produced; the king took him in his arms and returned to his palace, and the people of the country celebrated. Since the baby would not drink milk, the king feared he would not live long, so he soon returned to the divine shrine to pray again for a way to nourish him. The ground in front of the deity suddenly rose up in the shape of a breast, and the divine child suckled from it until he grew to adulthood. His wisdom and courage surpassed his predecessors, and his moral influence spread far and wide; he then built a divine shrine to honor his ancestor. From that time on, the throne has been passed down through generations, and the kings have ruled the country without the line being broken. Therefore, the divine temple today contains many precious treasures, and offerings and sacrifices are made there without fail. Because he was nourished by the earth-breast, this became the name of the country.

zh: 王城南十餘里有大伽藍，此國先王為毘盧折那（唐言遍照）阿羅漢建也。昔者，此國佛法未被，而阿羅漢自迦濕彌羅國至此林中，宴坐習定。時有見者，駭其容服，具以其狀上白於王。王遂躬往，觀其容止，曰：「爾何人乎，獨在幽林？」羅漢曰：「我，如來弟子，閑居習定。王宜樹福，弘讚佛教，建伽藍，召僧眾。」王曰：「如來者，有何德，有何神，而汝鳥棲，勤苦奉教？」曰：「如來慈愍四生，誘導三界，或顯或隱，示生示滅。遵其法者，出離生死，迷其教者，羈纏愛網。」王曰：「誠如所說，事高言議，既云大聖，為我現形；既得瞻仰，當為建立，罄心歸信，弘揚教法。」羅漢曰：「王建伽藍，功成感應。」王苟從其請，建僧伽藍，遠近咸集，法會稱慶，而未有揵稚扣擊召集。王謂羅漢曰：「伽藍已成，佛在何所？」羅漢曰：「當至誠，聖鑒不遠。」王遂禮請，忽見空中佛像下降，授王揵稚，因即誠信，弘揚佛教。
en_current: More than ten li to the south of the royal city is a great monastery, which was built by a former king of this country for the Arhat Vairocana (meaning "Universal Shining" in Chinese). In the past, the Buddha’s teaching had not yet reached this country, but the Arhat came from the country of Kaśmīra to this forest, where he sat in quietude to practice meditation. At that time, those who saw him were startled by his appearance and attire, and they reported his condition in detail to the king. The king then went in person to observe his demeanor and said, "Who are you, staying alone in this secluded forest?" The Arhat replied, "I am a disciple of the Tathāgata, living in seclusion to practice meditation. Your Majesty should cultivate merit, propagate the Buddha’s teaching, build a monastery, and assemble the monkhood." The king asked, "What virtues and divine powers does the Tathāgata possess that you would dwell like a bird in the woods and so diligently follow his teachings?" He replied, "The Tathāgata compassionately cares for the four types of birth and guides the three realms; he sometimes manifests and sometimes remains hidden, demonstrating birth and demonstrating extinction. Those who follow his teaching escape birth and death; those who are confused by his teaching remain entangled in the net of desire." The king said, "If it is truly as you say, the matter transcends words and discussion. Since you speak of a Great Sage, manifest his form for me; once I have been able to gaze upon him, I shall build [a monastery], devote my heart to faith, and propagate the teaching." The Arhat said, "If the king builds a monastery, the merit will bring about a response." The king followed his request and built a sanghārāma; people from far and near gathered to celebrate the dharma assembly, but they lacked a ghaṇṭā to strike for summoning the assembly. The king said to the Arhat, "The monastery (saṃghārāma) is now completed, but where is the Buddha?" The Arhat replied, "You must be perfectly sincere; the Sage’s observation is not far off." The king then performed rites of petition, and suddenly he saw an image of the Buddha descend from the air and bestow upon the king a ghaṇṭā (揵稚). Because of this, he became sincerely faithful and propagated the Buddha’s teaching.

zh: 王城西南二十餘里，有瞿室𩜁伽山（唐言牛角）。山峯兩起，巖隒四絕，於崖谷間建一伽藍，其中佛像時燭光明。昔如來曾至此處，為諸天、人略說法要，懸記此地當建國土，敬崇遺法，遵習大乘。牛角山巖有大石室，中有阿羅漢，入滅心定，待慈氏佛，數百年間，供養無替。近者崖崩，掩塞門徑，國王興兵欲除崩石，即黑蜂群飛，毒螫人眾，以故至今石門不開。
en_current: More than twenty li to the southwest of the royal city is the mountain of Gośṛṅga (瞿室𩜁伽山; in the language of Tang, "Cow Horn"). Two peaks rise up, and the rocky precipices are sheer on all sides. A monastery (saṃghārāma) is built between the cliffs and the valley, where the Buddha image within occasionally radiates light. In the past, the Tathāgata came to this place to briefly explain the essential Dharma for the various devas and humans, and he prophesied that a kingdom would be established here that would revere and honor the remaining Dharma and follow the practice of the Great Vehicle (Mahāyāna). In the rocky cliffs of Mount Cow Horn, there is a large stone chamber where an arhat resides, having entered the samadhi of extinction to await the Buddha Maitreya; for several hundred years, offerings to him have never ceased. Recently, the cliff collapsed and blocked the entrance path. The king mobilized troops to clear away the fallen stones, but immediately a swarm of black wasps flew out and stung the people, and for this reason, the stone gate has not been opened to this day.

zh: 王城西南十餘里，有地迦婆縛那伽藍。中有夾紵立佛像，本從屈支國而來至止。昔此國中有臣被譴，寓居屈支，恒禮此像。後蒙還國，傾心遙敬，夜分之後，像忽自至，其人捨宅，建此伽藍。
en_current: More than ten *li* to the southwest of the royal city, there is the Dīrghabhāvana Monastery (地迦婆縛那伽藍). Inside is a standing Buddha image made of hollow lacquer, which originally came here from the country of Kuci (屈支國). Formerly, a minister of this country was banished and lived in Kuci, where he constantly worshipped this image. Later, after he was allowed to return to his country, he continued to venerate it from afar with all his heart. After midnight, the image suddenly arrived of its own accord, and the man gave up his residence to build this monastery.

zh: 王城西行三百餘里，至勃伽夷城。中有佛坐像，高七尺餘，相好允備，威肅嶷然，首戴寶冠，光明時照。聞諸土俗曰：本在迦濕彌羅國，請移至此。昔有羅漢，其沙彌弟子臨命終時，求酢米餅。羅漢以天眼觀，見瞿薩旦那國有此味焉，運神通力，至此求獲。沙彌噉已，願生其國，果遂宿心，得為王子。既嗣位已，威攝遐邇，遂踰雪山，伐迦濕彌羅國。迦濕彌羅國王整集戎馬，欲禦邊寇。時阿羅漢諫王：「勿鬪兵也，我能退之。」尋為瞿薩旦那王說諸法要。王初未信，尚欲興兵。羅漢遂取此王先身沙彌時衣，而以示之。王既見衣，得宿命智，與迦濕彌羅王謝咎交歡，釋兵而返，奉迎沙彌時所供養佛像，隨軍禮請。像至此地，不可轉移，環建伽藍，或招僧侶，捨寶冠置像頂，今所冠者，即先王所施也。
en_current: Traveling three hundred-odd *li* west from the royal city, one arrives at the city of Bhagai (勃伽夷城). Within it is a seated image of the Buddha, over seven feet high. Its physical marks are perfectly complete, and its majestic, solemn appearance is awe-inspiring. It wears a precious crown on its head, which emits light from time to time. According to local tradition, it was originally in the country of Kaśmīra (迦濕彌羅國) and was invited to be moved here. Long ago, there was an arhat whose *śrāmaṇera* (novice) disciple, when approaching the end of his life, asked for some sour rice cakes. The arhat used his heavenly eye to observe and saw that this delicacy existed in the country of Gostāna (瞿薩旦那國); he employed his supernatural powers to travel there and obtain it. After the *śrāmaṇera* had eaten it, he wished to be reborn in that country. His past aspiration was fulfilled, and he became the prince. Once he had succeeded to the throne, his might intimidated both near and far; he then crossed the Snow Mountains (Himālaya) to invade the country of Kaśmīra. The King of Kaśmīra mobilized his troops and horses, intending to resist the border invaders. At that time, the arhat admonished the king, saying, "Do not engage in battle; I can cause them to retreat." He then explained the essential teachings of the Dharma to the King of Gostāna. The king did not believe him at first and still wished to raise his army. The arhat then took the robe that this king had worn in his previous life as a *śrāmaṇera* and showed it to him. Once the king saw the robe, he attained the knowledge of past lives; he apologized to the King of Kaśmīra, reconciled with him, and released his troops to return home. He respectfully invited the Buddha image that he had worshipped when he was a *śrāmaṇera* to follow his army. When the image reached this place, it could not be moved further, so they built a monastery around it and invited monks to reside there. The king offered his precious crown and placed it upon the head of the image; the crown it wears today is the very one bestowed by the former king.

zh: 王城西百五六十里，大沙磧正路中，有堆阜，並鼠壤墳也。聞之土俗曰：此沙磧中，鼠大如蝟，其毛則金銀異色，為其群之酋長，每出穴遊止，則群鼠為從。昔者，匈奴率數十萬眾，寇掠邊城，至鼠墳側屯軍，時瞿薩旦那王率數萬兵，恐力不敵，素知磧中鼠奇，而未神也。洎乎寇至，無所求救，君臣震恐，莫知圖計。苟復設祭，焚香請鼠，冀其有靈，少加軍力。其夜瞿薩旦那王夢見大鼠。曰：「敬欲相助。願早治兵，旦日合戰，必當克勝。」瞿薩旦那王知有靈祐，遂整戎馬，申令將士，未明而行，長驅掩襲。匈奴之聞也，莫不懼焉。方欲駕乘被鎧，而諸馬鞍、人服、弓弦、甲縺，凡厥帶系，鼠皆齧斷。兵寇既臨，面縛受戮。於是殺其將，虜其兵，匈奴震懾，以為神靈所祐也。瞿薩旦那王感鼠厚恩，建祠設祭，奕世遵敬，特深珍異。故上自君王，下至黎庶，咸修祀祭，以求福祐。行次其穴，下乘而趨，拜以致敬，祭以祈福。或衣服、弓、矢，或香花、肴膳，亦既輸誠，多蒙福利。若無享祭，則逢災變。
en_current: One hundred and fifty or sixty li to the west of the royal city, in the middle of the main road through the great desert, there are mounds which are all rat-earth hillocks (鼠壤墳). According to local tradition, in this desert there are rats as large as hedgehogs, whose fur is of various colors of gold and silver. They are the leaders of their groups, and whenever they emerge from their burrows to roam or rest, the other rats follow them.  In the past, the Xiongnu led several hundred thousand troops to invade and plunder the frontier cities, stationing their army beside these rat mounds. At that time, the King of Gostana (瞿薩旦那王) led several tens of thousands of soldiers, fearing that his strength was no match for the enemy. He had long known that the rats in the desert were remarkable, but he had not yet regarded them as divine. When the invaders arrived, there was nowhere to seek help, and the king and his ministers were terrified, not knowing what strategy to devise. In desperation, he set up offerings, burned incense, and petitioned the rats, hoping that they possessed spiritual power and would add a little to his military strength.  That night, the King of Gostana saw a giant rat in a dream. It said, "I wish to assist you. Prepare your troops early, and when you engage in battle at daybreak, you will surely be victorious." The King of Gostana, knowing he had received divine protection, immediately readied his horses and weapons and issued orders to his officers and men. Before dawn, they marched out and launched a surprise attack. When the Xiongnu heard of this, they were all struck with fear. Just as they were about to mount their horses and put on their armor, the rats gnawed through all their saddles, clothing, bowstrings, armor straps, and every kind of belt and fastening. When the enemy troops arrived, the Xiongnu stood with their hands bound behind their backs, waiting to be executed. Thereupon, the king killed their generals and captured their soldiers. The Xiongnu were terrified, believing that the king was protected by divine spirits.
